articles.title: Securitize Agrees to Buy River One as Q3 Revenue Rises 13%
articles.excerpt: The tokenization firm also posted a $66.3 million net loss, about $60 million of it from listing-related charges, and approved a $50 million buyback.
articles.body_md:
Securitize, the company that puts funds and stocks on blockchains for managers like BlackRock and ARK Invest, agreed Monday to buy lender River One and reported third-quarter revenue of $18.6 million, up 13% from a year earlier. Its shares rose about 10% after hours, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/tokenization-platform-securitize-reports-gains-expands-into-asset-backed-finance.html).

The deal moves Securitize from issuing tokens to lending against assets. River One, founded in New York in 2025, does warehouse financing: short-term credit that lenders use to fund new loans, backed by pools of small-business loans, receivables and similar assets, [Securitize said](https://investors.securitize.io/news/news-details/2026/Securitize-to-Acquire-River-One-Connecting-Stablecoin-Capital-to-the-6-Trillion-Asset-Backed-Finance-Market/default.aspx). Terms weren't disclosed. The company expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter.

**Two ways the business gets paid**

Tokenizing a fund means issuing a blockchain token that stands for a share in it, so it can move and settle around the clock. Securitize charges for that work, and it also earns by running fund back offices. Per its [results release](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/securitize-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-302933834.html), tokenization revenue rose 28% to $11.5 million while asset-servicing revenue fell 6% to $7.2 million.

Tokenized assets on the platform stood at $4.8 billion on Sept. 30, up 9%. The quarterly average was a company-record $5.0 billion.

**The loss behind the growth**

Net loss was $66.3 million, or 41 cents a share, after a $4.1 million profit a year earlier. The company said about $60 million of the loss came from largely non-cash charges tied to its July listing on the NYSE through a merger with Cantor Equity Partners II. Operating costs rose 183% to $42.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA, which leaves those charges out, was a $2.0 million loss.

The board approved buybacks of up to $50 million through Dec. 31, 2027. Securitize ended September with about $298.9 million in cash and no debt. Its release lists the risk that the River One deal doesn't close on the expected terms or timeline, or at all.

*In our opinion: the line to follow is asset servicing, the only revenue stream that shrank, as assets under administration fell 29% to $25.2 billion. Securitize is leaning on token fees to carry growth while it adds a lending arm on top. The fourth-quarter closing date for River One is the first checkpoint.*

articles.title: Schwab Crypto Adds Solana, Avalanche and Chainlink Trading
articles.excerpt: The brokerage's crypto menu grows from two tokens to five. Every trade costs 0.75% of its dollar value, and accounts aren't offered in New York or Louisiana.
articles.body_md:
Charles Schwab clients can now buy and sell solana, avalanche and chainlink, the brokerage [said Monday](https://pressroom.aboutschwab.com/press-releases/press-release/2026/Charles-Schwab-Makes-Solana-Avalanche-and-Chainlink-Available-to-Trade-Through-Schwab-Crypto-Accounts/default.aspx), taking its Schwab Crypto service from two tokens to five.

Until now, Schwab's direct crypto offer was bitcoin and ether. The three new listings are its first beyond those two.

**What clients pay**

Schwab charges 75 basis points, or 0.75%, on the dollar value of each trade. On a $1,000 purchase, that's $7.50. The coins sit in the same view as stocks and funds on Schwab.com, the Schwab Mobile app and thinkorswim, the company's trading platform.

Per the release's disclosures, the accounts are run by Charles Schwab Premier Bank, and the crypto in them isn't FDIC-insured or SIPC-protected (the two programs that cover bank deposits and brokerage accounts). Schwab Crypto isn't available in New York, Louisiana or U.S. territories.

**Three different jobs**

The new tokens do different things. Solana and Avalanche are blockchains that run apps and payments, and SOL and AVAX pay their fees. Chainlink is an oracle network, a service that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain apps; LINK pays its node operators.

At 5:55 p.m. ET, solana traded near $86.89, avalanche near $8.64 and chainlink near $10.69, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/solana).

**A slow, staged rollout**

Schwab Crypto opened to early-access clients in May and to all eligible retail clients in October. The company first said in late August it would add these three tokens, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/schwab-opens-solana-avalanche-and-chainlink-trading-to-its-retail-crypto-clients/), without a date.

"We continue to expand Schwab Crypto to give clients greater choice and flexibility," said Joe Vietri, Schwab's head of digital assets. The release said more assets will come over time but didn't name any.

*In our opinion: Schwab adds coins the way it adds anything, carefully and with a long disclosure page attached. About 11 weeks passed between the August plan and Monday's listings. The number to keep an eye on is that 0.75% fee, because it's what clients pay on every trade and what Schwab earns, and the next listing announcement will show whether the menu keeps growing.*

articles.title: October CPI Will Skip the Annual Inflation Rate, BLS Says
articles.excerpt: The 12-month rate was 3.7% in September. Tuesday's report will show only monthly changes, because October 2025 prices were never collected.
articles.body_md:
Tuesday's consumer price report will arrive without its best-known number. The Bureau of Labor Statistics won't publish 12-month changes for most October CPI series, including headline and core, when the report comes out at 8:30 a.m. ET, [the agency says](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/additional-resources/2025-federal-government-shutdown-impact-cpi-faq.htm).

That annual rate is the figure most people mean by inflation. In September it was 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August, with core prices (everything but food and energy) up 2.6%, per the [September CPI release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm).

**Why the number is missing**

The CPI tracks what a fixed basket of goods and services costs each month and turns it into an index. The 12-month change compares this October's index with last October's. There is no last October. During the 2025 government shutdown, which ran Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, BLS stopped collecting prices, carried September's forward to fill the gap and never published most October 2025 indexes.

BLS laid out the plan in a shutdown FAQ last updated Sept. 16. Bloomberg reported Monday that the October report would leave out both annual figures, [Quartz said](https://qz.com/bls-skip-12-month-cpi-october-inflation-report-110926).

**Monthly figures still come out**

Economists in the Dow Jones survey expect prices rose 0.3% in October and core 0.2%, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/october-cpi-report-2026-inflation.html). September's gains were 0.6% and 0.3%. Energy prices were up 20.4% over the year to September, and gasoline alone made up more than half of September's monthly rise, BLS said.

Fed officials are already talking about prices. "We've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday, per CNBC.

Bitcoin traded near $75,190 at 5:55 p.m. ET, up 1.1% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

Any October annual rate quoted Tuesday will be someone else's calculation, not a BLS figure. The November report is scheduled for Dec. 10.

articles.title: NYSE Picks Avalanche Ledger to Clear Its Planned Tokenized Stock Venue
articles.excerpt: Avalanche will run the ledger behind the clearing firm for an NYSE-affiliated trading system planned for 24/7 trading. It still needs regulatory approval.
articles.body_md:
The New York Stock Exchange has picked Avalanche to supply the core ledger for the clearing firm behind its planned tokenized stock venue, [Avalanche said in a blog post](https://www.avalanche.com/about/blog/wall-streets-next-chapter-is-being-built-on-avalanche) on Monday, Nov. 9. The NYSE flagged the deal in its [pre-market update](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/avalanche-to-support-nyses-affiliated-upcoming-digital-ats-nyse-content-update-302933387.html) the same morning.

The venue will be an alternative trading system (ATS), a privately run market that trades securities under SEC rules without being a full exchange. Neither company gave a launch date, and the venue still needs regulators to sign off.

**Where the blockchain sits**

Trading a stock has two halves. First, an engine matches a buyer with a seller. Then comes clearing and settlement, the step where shares and cash actually change owners, with a clearing firm standing between the two sides until it's done.

That second half is the part moving onto Avalanche. The NYSE's [January announcement](https://ir.theice.com/press/news-details/2026/The-New-York-Stock-Exchange-Develops-Tokenized-Securities-Platform/) from parent Intercontinental Exchange said the platform would pair its Pillar matching engine with blockchain-based post-trade systems, aiming for 24/7 trading, instant settlement, orders sized in dollars and funding in stablecoins. It also said tokenized shareholders would keep dividends and voting rights.

According to Avalanche, Dennis Lee, the NYSE's head of digital issuance, said the settlement ledger had to be fast, reliable, predictable in cost and able to control who takes part. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382833/nyse-avalanche-settle-tokenized-stock-platform) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/09/nyse-picks-avalanche-to-settle-tokenized-stocks-amid-wall-street-s-blockchain-race) also reported that the venue is designed to accept stocks issued on other blockchains.

**What the posts leave out**

Neither the Avalanche post nor the NYSE update gives fees, the name of the clearing firm, trading volumes or a timetable. AVAX, Avalanche's token, traded at $8.73 at 11:55 a.m. ET, up 6.9% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/avalanche).

*In our opinion: the bigger story is which layer moved. Tokenized funds such as BlackRock's BUIDL already sit on Avalanche, Avalanche says, but this puts a blockchain under the step where ownership changes hands for an NYSE venue. The document worth waiting for is the regulatory filing, because that's where fees, the clearing firm and a start date have to show up.*

articles.title: PNC Lets Corporate Clients Take USDC Payments, Paid Out in Dollars
articles.excerpt: The pilot runs on Coinbase's payment tools and Ethereum. PNC hasn't named the clients taking part, the price, or when it might open more widely.
articles.body_md:
PNC Bank's corporate clients can now get paid in USDC and find U.S. dollars in their account. The Pittsburgh bank [announced the pilot](https://pnc.mediaroom.com/2026-11-09-PNC-Bank-Launches-Incoming-Stablecoin-Payments-for-Corporate-and-Institutional-Banking-Clients) on Monday, Nov. 9, built on Coinbase's payment products.

For a business with customers or suppliers abroad, it's a way to accept a digital dollar without holding crypto. Incoming USDC on Ethereum is converted 1-to-1 into dollars and deposited into a designated PNC account, the bank said.

**How the payment works**

USDC is a stablecoin, a token meant to hold a steady $1 value. Its issuer, Circle, calls it "a fully reserved digital dollar" on its [USDC page](https://www.circle.com/usdc). A payer sends the token over a blockchain at any hour, and stablecoins can be sent and received almost instantly, Reuters noted. In PNC's setup, the client never ends up holding the token: Coinbase handles the crypto side and PNC books the dollars.

About $70.4 billion of USDC was in circulation on Monday, per [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins).

"Right now, this is about testing and learning with our clients," Tom Lang, PNC's head of Treasury Management product and operations, told [Reuters](https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4003973-pnc-to-offerstablecoin-payments-to-clients-in-coinbase-partnership). Alec Lovett, Coinbase's head of infrastructure products, said in the release that stablecoins make business payments "faster, more efficient and more global."

**Built on an older deal**

PNC first tied up with Coinbase in July 2025 and began offering spot bitcoin trading to eligible private banking clients in December, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-09-coinbase-pnc-bank-expand-partnership-with-usdc-payments-corporate-clients-436466) reported. This pilot is open only to eligible corporate and institutional clients. Neither company disclosed fees, the clients taking part or volumes.

*In our opinion: the detail worth chasing is the fee. PNC hasn't said what it charges to turn a stablecoin into a deposit, and that price decides whether a treasury team picks USDC over a wire. The pilot only covers money coming in, so the next real step to watch is whether PNC lets clients send USDC out.*

articles.title: Strategy Pays $79,012 a Coin for 1,036 Bitcoin, Above Its Own Average
articles.excerpt: More of the week's stock-sale money went to buying back STRC preferred shares: $188.3 million, against $81.9 million for bitcoin.
articles.body_md:
Strategy bought 1,036 bitcoin last week at an average of $79,012 each, pricier than the $75,456 it has paid on average for its whole stack, its [Form 8-K filed Monday](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526452693/mstr-20261109.htm) shows.

That means the newest coins are already worth less than they cost. Bitcoin traded near $74,950 at 11:55 a.m. ET on Monday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). Black Mint [reported Sunday](https://blackmint.markets/news/bitcoin-below-strategy-average-cost/) that bitcoin had slipped below Strategy's average cost; the new buy nudged that average up by $5.

**The money went somewhere else first**

Strategy raised $283.8 million after commissions by selling 2,051,348 Class A shares through its at-the-market program, which lets a company sell new stock straight into the market a little at a time. Only $81.9 million of that, about 29%, bought bitcoin.

The largest slice, $188.3 million, went to buying back 1,887,464 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock. That works out to about $99.76 a share, [Unchained calculated](https://unchainedcrypto.com/strategy-buys-1036-btc-but-spends-more-repurchasing-its-preferred-stock-just-under-100/). Preferred stock gets its dividend paid before common shareholders see anything. STRC's rate is variable, and Executive Chairman Michael Saylor has said Strategy aims to keep its price between $99 and $100, Unchained reported.

The last $13.6 million went to "USD Cash," the company's general-purpose pot.

**Where the stack stands**

- Holdings: 850,364 BTC as of Nov. 8
- Total cost: $64.16 billion, including fees
- Value at $74,948 a coin: about $63.7 billion, roughly $430 million below cost
- USD Reserve for dividends and interest: $4.77 billion, after $21.1 million in preferred dividends last week

The filing reports no bitcoin sales. Strategy has $560.3 million left under its preferred buyback program.

*In our opinion: for a company built to buy bitcoin, spending more than twice as much on its own preferred shares is the line in this filing that deserves the attention. Holders of the common stock are funding both moves, and the $4.77 billion reserve is what covers the preferred dividends while bitcoin sits under cost. The 1,036 new coins began their Strategy careers about $4,000 each under water, so next Monday's 8-K will show whether the buyback pace holds.*

articles.title: Binance Pool Mines One Bitcoin Block in a Week Before Tuesday Shutdown
articles.excerpt: Miners still pointed at Binance Pool have until 2 a.m. ET Tuesday to switch. Pool Savings and Cloud Mining close at the same time.
articles.body_md:
Binance Pool found one of the 916 bitcoin blocks mined over the past week, about 0.11%, [mempool.space data](https://mempool.space/mining/pool/binancepool) showed at 6:04 a.m. ET Monday. The pool shuts at 07:00 UTC Tuesday, which is 2 a.m. ET.

Any miner still connected after that time earns nothing for the work. Binance's [Oct. 13 notice](https://tokenearly.com/announcement/6acd9ebaef4bd2e7553de33d.html) says shares submitted after the cutoff "will no longer be accepted, processed, or credited."

**How a mining pool pays**

A single machine almost never finds a block on its own. A pool combines thousands of miners' computing power, and when any of them finds a block, the reward (3.125 new bitcoin plus fees) is split by how much work each one sent. Miners can point the same machines at a different pool by changing one server address, without turning anything off.

Binance Pool's last block was No. 974,743, found at 9:15 p.m. ET on Nov. 5 with 1,353 transactions, per mempool.space. It found none in the latest 24 hours. Over its life it has mined 22,213 blocks, the same data show.

Bitcoin.com News [reported](https://news.bitcoin.com/mining/binance-pulls-plug-bitcoin-mining-after-6-year-run/) on Oct. 13 that the pool, launched in April 2020, was the ninth-largest by hashrate and was mining about three blocks a day. Binance's notice gave no reason for the closure.

**What else closes, and what to save**

Pool Savings, Cloud Mining, the Transaction Accelerator and the pool's API and alerts all end at the same cutoff. Binance tells users to redeem Pool Savings positions before then and to finish any identity checks by 23:59 UTC Tuesday so leftover rewards can be paid.

The week's block count also shows where the hashrate sits now. Foundry USA found 227 blocks, AntPool 173 and F2Pool 160, mempool.space shows. A week with one block is a small sample, and block luck swings, so it can't pin down how much computing power is still connected to Binance Pool.

Binance Pool's history pages, including payout records, stay viewable until 07:00 UTC on Nov. 24. After that, Binance says, they go offline for good.

articles.title: Galxe Shuts Quest, ID and Passport, Sets Dec. 15 Reward Deadline
articles.excerpt: Galxe says it served 36 million users. Campaigns end Dec. 5, and staked G and Smart Savings balances will get a separate claim process later.
articles.body_md:
Galxe users have until Dec. 15 to claim any campaign rewards. After that, the whole Galxe website goes read-only, the company [said on X](https://x.com/Galxe/status/2119681030609105175) at 1:38 a.m. ET Monday as it folds its team and brand into Gravity, its own blockchain.

Galxe Quest, Galxe ID, Galxe Passport and related services are being wound down. The last day to take part in any campaign is Dec. 5.

**How Galxe campaigns worked**

Galxe ran quest campaigns for crypto projects: a project posted tasks, such as making an on-chain transaction or following an account, and users who finished them earned rewards. Galxe ID and Passport handled identity and credentials behind those campaigns. The company says it served 36 million users and more than 7,700 partner projects over five-plus years.

**What stopped Monday**

Some of it ended right away. Starting Monday, Spaces (the project pages) can no longer create new campaigns, and new Galxe+ and Galxe Score subscriptions and Passport minting are closed, the post says.

Gravity, the network, keeps running, and the company said there are "no changes to the G token as part of this transition." G is the gas token on Gravity L1, [Crypto Briefing reported](https://cryptobriefing.com/galxe-consolidates-gravity-l1-quest-shutdown/).

**Some balances wait for a second notice**

Three kinds of assets are not on the December timetable: Smart Savings balances, staked G not yet withdrawn, and G held in wallets on Gravity Alpha Mainnet. Galxe says these "remain safe" and will follow a separate claim process, with details in a later post on X. It gave no date for that post.

That older network is already gone. Gravity Alpha Mainnet shut down on Nov. 1 after a bridging window that ran Oct. 23-25, Crypto Briefing reported, and Galxe had [warned users on X](https://x.com/Galxe/status/2113799196406915097) in October to move funds off the network before those deadlines.

Galxe's post does not say how many users still hold unclaimed rewards or how much those rewards are worth.

The next dates are fixed: campaigns close Dec. 5, and reward claims close Dec. 15.

articles.title: Coinbase Wins Full OCC Trust Charter for Custody, Not Deposits
articles.excerpt: The federal charter covers custody, not deposits or loans. Coinbase plans to move its New York custody business into the new bank over three years.
articles.body_md:
Coinbase now runs a national trust bank. The exchange said Monday that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has granted final approval for Coinbase National Trust Company, turning the conditional charter it won on April 2 into a full one, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/09/coinbase-gets-full-u-s-trust-charter-from-federal-banking-regulator) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/coinbase-full-us-trust-charter-occ/) reported.

For institutions that keep crypto with Coinbase, the custodian moves under a federal bank supervisor instead of relying on a New York State license alone.

**How a trust charter differs from a bank**

A national trust bank holds and safeguards assets for clients as a fiduciary, meaning it must act in their interest. It does not take retail deposits or make loans. The OCC's [April approval letter](https://www.occ.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/interpretations-and-decisions/2026/cd1370.pdf) describes the new bank's job as digital asset custody, "primarily for institutional clients," plus letting custody customers hold and transfer cash and coins in their accounts. Cash held in custody sits in "for benefit of" accounts at other banks, the letter says.

The reports of Monday's approval don't say how many client assets the new bank will hold on day one. For scale, OCC-supervised uninsured national trust banks reported $1.7 trillion in custody and safekeeping accounts as of Dec. 31, 2025, the letter says.

**Staking stays with affiliates**

The letter sets limits. Custody clients can reach Coinbase's staking, Prime Trading and Prime Financing products, but the bank acts only as a finder: affiliates provide those services, not the bank itself. Coinbase will move the whole custody business from Coinbase Custody Trust Company, its New York-chartered trust firm, to the national bank over the three-year start-up period, according to the letter.

Coinbase's [April blog post](https://www.coinbase.com/blog/coinbase-receives-conditional-occ-approval-building-the-future-of-finance) said the company would not take retail deposits or engage in fractional reserve banking, and that its BitLicense and New York trust charter stay in place.

Ripple won its own final OCC trust approval on Oct. 26, Crypto Briefing reported.

*In our opinion: the line to watch is the three-year migration. Until the custody book actually moves, Coinbase runs two regulators' rulebooks side by side. The next checkable document is the OCC's own final-approval record, and whether it attaches conditions beyond April's.*

articles.title: Emirates NBD's Liv Adds USDU, a Central Bank-Registered Dollar Token
articles.excerpt: Liv has close to half a million users and is waiving crypto trading fees for 90 days. UAE rules limit USDU to paying for digital assets.
articles.body_md:
Liv, the digital bank run by Emirates NBD, is adding USDU, a U.S. dollar stablecoin registered by the Central Bank of the UAE, to its app, the companies said in a [press release](https://www.zawya.com/en/press-release/companies-news/liv-by-emirates-nbd-universal-and-aquanow-to-deliver-the-first-integration-of-a-cbuae-registered-usd-backed-stablecoin-2127691) on Monday. To launch it, Liv is waiving crypto trading fees for 90 days.

Liv has close to half a million users, the release says. Its crypto service, Liv X, already runs on Aquanow, a Dubai-licensed broker that says it has processed more than $130 billion in trading volume.

**What the token can and can't do**

A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a fixed value, here $1, backed by cash held elsewhere. Under the UAE's Payment Token Services Regulation, payments for digital assets in the country can only be made in regular money or a registered foreign payment token, [Universal said](https://www.universal.ae/news/universal-launches-uaes-first-central-bank-registered-usd-stablecoin) when it launched USDU on Jan. 29. USDU was the first token registered that way.

The flip side: USDU "may not be used for general payment purposes in the UAE," Universal's launch notice says. Monday's release repeats that it is not a general-purpose domestic payment instrument. In practice, it is a dollar balance for buying and selling crypto.

**Who holds the dollars**

Universal, the ADGM-regulated issuer, says each token is backed 1:1 by dollars in onshore accounts at Emirates NBD and Mashreq, with monthly attestations by an outside accounting firm. That puts Emirates NBD on both ends: it safeguards part of the reserves and now sells the token to its own app customers, [tbreak reported](https://tbreak.com/liv-usdu-stablecoin-uae/).

Rohit Garg, Emirates NBD's chief digital officer for retail banking, said in the release that USDU gives customers a "secure, transparent and regulated bridge to digital assets" inside their everyday banking app.

The release does not say when USDU goes live in the app, what fees apply after the 90 days, or whether users can send it to outside wallets. It also gives no figure for how many USDU tokens exist.

*In our opinion: Emirates NBD now sits on both sides of this token, holding part of the reserves and selling USDU in its own app, which makes Universal's monthly attestations the document worth reading. Monday's release gives no supply figure, so the next attestation is the place to check how many tokens exist. The 90-day fee holiday is generous; the more telling number arrives on day 91.*

articles.title: China's Producer Prices Rise 5.7% While Consumer Inflation Cools
articles.excerpt: Coal mining prices jumped 36.6% from a year earlier while food fell 2.9%. Beijing also kept its extra 24% tariff on U.S. goods suspended for two more months.
articles.body_md:
China's factory-gate prices rose 5.7% in October from a year earlier, the National Bureau of Statistics said at 9:30 a.m. Beijing time Monday (8:30 p.m. ET Sunday). Consumer inflation went the other way, slowing to 0.7%.

The producer figure beat the 5.3% that economists polled by Reuters expected, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/china-wholesale-inflation-rises-consumer.html), and was the fastest pace since June 2022. It was the third month in a row of faster gains. The bureau said the rate widened 0.7 percentage point from September, which puts September at 5.0%.

**What the producer index measures**

The producer price index, or PPI, tracks what Chinese factories charge when goods first leave the plant. The bureau surveys prices for more than 1,300 product categories across 41 industries. Read next to consumer prices, it shows where costs are building inside supply chains, from raw materials to finished goods.

**Coal and oil did most of the lifting**

Mining prices were up 27.9% from a year earlier and raw materials 11.6%, the [bureau's PPI release](https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfbhjd/202611/t20261109_1965794.html) shows. Coal mining rose 36.6%. Oil and gas extraction rose 35.0%. Prices factories paid for their own inputs climbed 7.9%. Chief statistician Dong Lijuan [said](https://www1.xinhuanet.com/fortune/20261109/decb1630fe0f4b03b1eedaed46676cc1/c.html) higher international energy prices drove most of October's 0.7% monthly rise.

Shoppers saw little of it. Food prices fell 2.9% from a year earlier, and core CPI, which strips out food and energy, eased to 0.8% from 1.0%. Economists polled by Reuters had expected headline CPI of 0.8%, CNBC reported.

**Beijing keeps the 24% tariff on hold**

The same day, China's Customs Tariff Commission [said](https://gss.mof.gov.cn/gzdt/zhengcefabu/202611/t20261109_4004260.htm) it will keep its extra 24% tariff on U.S. goods suspended for two more months from 1:01 p.m. Tuesday Beijing time, while a 10% extra tariff stays in place, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/china-extends-suspension-of-24-tariff-on-us-imports-for-two-months-5010427). Mainland China's CSI 300 index rose 0.56% after the inflation data, per CNBC.

Bitcoin was down 1.3% over 24 hours at $74,762 at 11:56 p.m. ET, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show.

*In our opinion: the number that matters is the five-point gap. Chinese factories are charging 5.7% more while shoppers pay 0.7% more, and the bureau's own breakdown puts most of the factory jump on coal and oil. The next checks are China's November figures and early January, when the two-month tariff pause runs out.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Under Strategy's $75,451 Average Cost Per Coin
articles.excerpt: Strategy's 849,327 BTC cost $64.08 billion and were worth about $63.4 billion Sunday evening. Reuters said bitcoin hit its lowest level since August.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell to about $74,650 on Sunday evening, below the $75,451 average price Strategy has paid for its coins. On those figures, the company's bitcoin stack is worth about $675 million less than it cost.

Strategy's [Nov. 2 filing with the SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526442707/mstr-20261102.htm) shows it held 849,327 BTC as of Nov. 1, bought for $64.08 billion including fees and expenses. At $74,653 per coin at 6:04 p.m. ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), those coins were worth about $63.4 billion. The filing is the latest holdings count we could find, so the real total may differ if Strategy bought more this week.

**How an average cost works**

Strategy has bought bitcoin in many batches at different prices. Its "average purchase price" is the total spent divided by the total coins held. When the market price sits below that number, the holding is worth less than was paid for it. That's a paper position: nothing is lost or locked in unless coins are sold, and the filing reports no sales.

**The move behind it**

Bitcoin was down 1.4% over 24 hours and 9.7% over 30 days at 6:04 p.m. ET, CoinGecko data show. [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/forex-news/cryptocurrencies-slide-to-twomonth-lows-after-us-midterms-5010335) that bitcoin dipped to $73,708 in late Sunday trade, the lowest since August, and that ether fell to $2,223. Reuters attributed the drop to investor worry that a Democratic-controlled Congress will toughen crypto regulation, and to the roughly $6 billion Binance theft.

At $73,708, the same 849,327 coins would be worth about $62.6 billion, or $1.5 billion below cost.

The last cost basis Strategy published was $80,846 per coin for the 811 BTC it added during the week of Oct. 26. Those newest coins were already above the market price.

*In our opinion: the line to check is Strategy's next weekly filing, which will show whether Strategy bought this week and at what price, which moves the $75,451 figure, even if only a little. A company that has put $64 billion into one asset keeps its scorecard in public, and this week the scorecard reads slightly red.*

articles.title: LNbits Tells Every Server Operator to Shut Down Pending Patches
articles.excerpt: The Lightning account system's developers say fixes should land in 24 to 48 hours. LNbits has not named the flaw or said how many servers were hit.
articles.body_md:
LNbits told everyone running its software to stop their servers immediately on Sunday, saying a wave of attacks had left it with security patches still to push. Contributor Ben Arc said the fixes should be merged and available within 24 to 48 hours.

The project's [8:56 a.m. ET post on X](https://x.com/lnbits/status/2119428804951048237) asked users to stop servers "IMMEDIATELY" and said, "it's better to err on the side of caution." Arc [added three minutes later](https://x.com/arcbtc/status/2119429503667642816) that operators should pass the warning on to anyone who might be running an instance. At 12:18 p.m. ET, LNbits [said](https://x.com/lnbits/status/2119479738783629384) it had switched off every instance on its own hosted service as a precaution and expected services to resume within 24 hours.

**From one extension to every server**

The warning widened through the morning. At 7:33 a.m. ET, LNbits had [asked operators](https://x.com/lnbits/status/2119408009700937798) with its Paywall extension enabled to turn it off while it investigated "a potential bug." The 8:56 a.m. post covered every server, with or without that extension.

**How LNbits works**

LNbits is open-source software that sits on top of a Lightning node and lets one operator give separate wallets to many users, with add-on extensions for things like paywalls and tipping. Because each server is connected to a node holding real bitcoin, a flaw in LNbits can reach that money. That's why the project is asking operators to stop servers rather than wait for a patch.

**A loss one operator reported**

Kevin Ravensberg, who runs the LNbits server behind the BitTipBot Telegram tipping bot, said newly created accounts withdrew 2,285,545 sats, about 0.023 bitcoin, from his server on Sunday before he stopped it, [Bitcoin.com News reported](https://news.bitcoin.com/security/lightning-network-security-scare-forces-lnbits-servers-offline/). It said he plans to cover the bot's users himself. We could not independently confirm the figure.

**What isn't known**

LNbits has not said what the vulnerabilities are, whether the Paywall bug is among them, how many servers were attacked, or how much was taken in total. Its latest tagged release on [GitHub](https://github.com/lnbits/lnbits/releases) is v1.6.2 from Sept. 18, and no new security advisory was listed when we checked at 6 p.m. ET.

Operators who stopped their servers should keep them off until a fixed release is published and LNbits says it is safe to restart.

articles.title: Binance Reopens HYPE and APT Withdrawals, Four of Six Still Pending
articles.excerpt: Binance said Friday it aimed to reopen six tokens by the end of next week. INJ, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC weren't on Sunday's list, 10 days after the $6.3 billion theft.
articles.body_md:
Binance reopened withdrawals for Hyperliquid's HYPE and Aptos' APT tokens at 3:52 a.m. ET Sunday, the exchange said in a [post on X](https://x.com/binance/status/2119352231732580574), ten days after the Oct. 29 theft of about $6.3 billion.

Those are two of the six tokens Binance named on Friday. In a [Nov. 6 post](https://x.com/binance/status/2118657118014496819), it said it was working to reopen HYPE, INJ, APT, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC "by end of next week," along with every token on networks already restored, including BSC, Ethereum, Arbitrum and Optimism.

**Four named tokens are still waiting**

Sunday's update lists HYPE and APT as new. It doesn't mention INJ, PLASMA, NEAR or LTC, and Binance hasn't given a date for them beyond Friday's target.

How does a withdrawal reopen one token at a time? When a customer withdraws, the exchange sends coins from its own wallets onto a specific blockchain. Each network has its own wallets, addresses and signing setup, so each route has to be checked separately before money moves again. That's why Binance's updates list assets network by network (five Ethereum stablecoins, including RLUSD and USD1, came back earlier).

**The money behind the restart**

Binance's [Recovery Update #7](https://x.com/binance/status/2118001921252347938) on Nov. 4 said 98% of the stolen assets were covered and came with an expanded proof-of-reserves snapshot. That is a published tally of what the exchange holds against what customers are owed at a single moment. Binance has said users won't bear the losses.

The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group for the attack, an allegation Pyongyang has denied, [Reuters reported](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/binance-cfo-kaiser-ng-steps-down-justin-yek-named-new-finance-chief-6533351).

HYPE was at $76.86 at 12:02 p.m. ET, down 0.6% in 24 hours, and APT was at $0.58, down 2.9%, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the count that matters now is four. Binance set its own deadline on Friday for INJ, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC, so the end of this coming week is the date to check. Customers holding those tokens on the exchange are still waiting on the one service a reserve snapshot can't replace: getting their coins out.*

articles.title: Keplr Says Some Emptied Balances Reflect Web3Auth Rescue Moves
articles.excerpt: Web3Auth posted the addresses holding rescued Keplr funds on 11 networks plus eight EVM chains. Neither firm has given a loss figure or a count of affected accounts.
articles.body_md:
Some Keplr wallets created with Google or Apple login may already show a reduced or empty balance because of rescue transfers, Keplr said in a [post on X](https://x.com/keplrwallet/status/2119117067500806350). At 1:23 a.m. ET Sunday, Web3Auth published the [recovery addresses](https://x.com/Web3Auth/status/2119314958236401922) holding those funds.

That matters for anyone who opened a Keplr wallet with a social login and saw coins leave. Web3Auth said some of its transfers "have been mistaken for attacker activity."

**How a rescue transfer works**

Web3Auth said Saturday that it and its partners had begun "whitehat recovery," aimed at wallets that were exposed but not yet drained, "utilizing the same path of the original attacker." In plain terms, defenders used the same weakness to move coins out first, into wallets they control, so an attacker couldn't reach them. Keplr described the flaw as a Web3Auth "infrastructure vulnerability leading to private key breach." Web3Auth runs the login service Keplr uses for Google and Apple sign-ins.

The list covers 11 networks, including Cosmos Hub, Osmosis, Celestia, Injective, dYdX and Noble, plus one address used on eight EVM chains, the networks that run Ethereum-style software. Web3Auth said it will add addresses as they are verified.

**What users were told to do**

Wallets made with a recovery phrase or a hardware device aren't affected, Keplr said. Social-login users were told not to send new funds to those accounts and to move any remaining liquid assets to a phrase or hardware wallet. Staked and locked tokens take longer to secure, Keplr said.

Neither company has said how many accounts were hit, how much was taken by the attacker or how much was moved to safety. Keplr said it is working with Web3Auth on a way for users to check whether their account is affected, and both said to trust only their official accounts and ignore "recovery" offers by DM.

*In our opinion: the address list is the most useful thing either company has published so far, because it lets users tell a rescue from a theft on-chain. The missing numbers are the next test. Until Web3Auth says how much it holds and how users get it back, affected holders can see where their coins went but not when they return.*

articles.title: Stablecoin Supply Falls to $292 Billion, Lowest in More Than a Year
articles.excerpt: Tether's USDT shed $2.8 billion in a week and Circle's USDC $1.2 billion as total supply slid for a fifth week, DefiLlama data show.
articles.body_md:
Stablecoin supply fell to $292.4 billion on Sunday, its lowest level since Sept. 24, 2025, [DefiLlama data](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) show. That's $6.6 billion less than on Oct. 31.

The slide has run for five weeks. DefiLlama's total stood at $307.9 billion on Oct. 7 and peaked at $315.5 billion on May 17, so about $23 billion has left the market since spring.

**Tether and Circle took most of the week's drop**

- Tether's USDT: down $2.8 billion in seven days, to $176.8 billion
- Circle's USDC: down $1.2 billion, to $70.6 billion
- World Liberty's USD1: down $430 million, to $3.45 billion

[CoinGecko's figures](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/tether) line up. USDT's market value slipped from $180.0 billion on Nov. 1 to $176.9 billion early Sunday, and [USDC's](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/usd-coin) went from $71.7 billion to $70.5 billion.

A few coins grew. Ethena's USDe added $431 million, to $4.93 billion, and Ripple's RLUSD added $274 million, to $2.69 billion, per DefiLlama.

**How a stablecoin shrinks**

A stablecoin is a token built to stay worth $1. Big issuers such as Tether and Circle mint new tokens when approved customers send in dollars, and burn them when customers cash out. Trading coins back and forth doesn't change the count. Supply falls only when more money is redeemed than deposited.

That makes the total a rough gauge of how many dollars are parked inside crypto, ready to trade or lend.

The data don't show who redeemed or why.

Prices barely moved on Sunday. Bitcoin sat near $75,820 at 5:55 a.m. ET, down 0.1% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko, after U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $411.9 million on Friday, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data show.

*In our opinion: the weekly change tells the story here. Five straight weeks of shrinking supply means more dollars are walking out than walking in, and USDT and USDC account for about $4 billion of this week's exits. The check-in worth making is Nov. 15, when a sixth weekly reading will show whether the exits slow or keep going.*

articles.title: OKX Asks Users to Stop Direct MEXC Transfers Ahead of FinCEN Cutoff
articles.excerpt: OKX CEO Star Xu said MEXC-linked funds get sanctions-style checks and possible freezes. FinCEN's 30-day clock hasn't started; OKX isn't waiting.
articles.body_md:
OKX founder and CEO Star Xu asked customers on Saturday to stop sending money straight from MEXC to OKX, two days after FinCEN's order against MEXC. "Please avoid transferring funds directly from MEXC to OKX," Xu [wrote on X](https://x.com/star_okx/status/2119203186074599424) at 5:59 p.m. ET.

Xu said OKX treats FinCEN special measures "with a level of caution similar to sanctions." Funds tied to affected platforms may be frozen, he wrote, with the related accounts open to further investigation. FinCEN allowed a 30-day transition, but OKX tightened its controls without waiting.

**A user's 860 USDT sat in review**

Xu was answering an [X user](https://x.com/HoppinsKarlz/status/2119017596796153998) who said deposits from their own MEXC account, 848.8 USDT on Tron and 11.7 USDT on Ethereum, were held for risk review after OKX flagged a "potentially high-risk address." [PANews](https://www.panews.io/articles/01a1b8ad-8362-7203-b2b9-3ffe90e0dbb4) and [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/okx-star-xu-avoid-mexc-transfers/) also reported Xu's remarks.

How does a deposit get stuck? Exchanges run incoming transfers through analytics tools that score the sending addresses. If a source is tied to a flagged platform, the deposit is parked while compliance staff ask where the money came from. FinCEN's order itself only bars covered U.S. financial institutions from moving funds to or from MEXC Global. OKX's step is its own policy.

Treasury [alleges](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0685) MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions from May 2021 to May 2026, as Black Mint reported Friday. The ban starts 30 days after the order is published in the Federal Register. It was not on the Register's [public inspection list](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/current) late Saturday ET.

**MEXC says it is operating normally**

MEXC said in a [statement](https://www.mexc.com/announcements/article/statement-regarding-fincen-s-november-6-order-17827791539626) that it is reviewing the order with its legal and compliance teams, that "user assets remain secure," and that it has begun an independent review of its anti-money-laundering and sanctions controls. CEO Vugar Usi said Saturday that deposits and withdrawals had not been suspended, [The Crypto Times reported](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/07/mexc-ceo-says-exchange-remains-live-after-us-treasury-ban/).

Xu did not say how many accounts or how much money OKX has held.

*In our opinion: the legal clock hasn't started, yet a major offshore exchange is already handling MEXC money the way it handles sanctioned money. That puts the first cost on ordinary MEXC customers, and Xu's own post allowed that a user hit by it could be "an innocent user caught up in this situation." Watch for the Federal Register notice, which starts the 30 days, and for any other exchange that posts similar deposit rules before it lands.*

articles.title: Sky's Savings Vault Sheds $571 Million in a Day at a 3.80% Rate
articles.excerpt: USDS supply also fell $805 million on the week to $5.59 billion, DefiLlama shows. Sky's savings rate never moved, and no one has said who withdrew.
articles.body_md:
Holders pulled about 571 million USDS out of Sky's savings vault in the 24 hours to 7 p.m. ET Friday, cutting deposits about 13% to 3.95 billion, [Aavescan's](https://aavescan.com/rates/sky-susds) daily reads of the vault contract show. The rate paid on those deposits stayed at 3.80%.

The drop shows up in the wider numbers too. Sky's total value locked fell to about $4.43 billion early Sunday from $5.23 billion a week earlier, and USDS circulating supply slid to $5.59 billion from $6.40 billion, [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/protocol/sky) data show. A direct read of the vault contract by Black Mint at about midnight ET Sunday returned 3.98 billion USDS.

**How the savings vault works**

USDS is Sky's dollar stablecoin, the successor to DAI. Holders who deposit USDS get sUSDS, a token that grows in value at the Sky Savings Rate. The rate is set by Sky governance and paid from the protocol's surplus, [TokenPost reported](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/47289), after governance raised it to 3.80% in October. On-chain data from [Chartegy](https://chartegy.com/data/series/SKY_SAVINGS_RATE) show it unchanged since at least Oct. 26.

Withdrawing swaps sUSDS back into USDS (the coins come out of the vault, they don't disappear). That alone doesn't shrink supply. Supply falls only when USDS is redeemed or burned, which is why the two figures moved by different amounts.

**Who moved the money is not known**

Neither data source identifies the wallets behind Friday's withdrawal. Sky's main X accounts had not posted about it through Saturday. On Nov. 6, the [Sky Ecosystem account](https://x.com/SkyEcosystem/status/2118697883121914148) posted about a $100 million sUSDS allocation from Galaxy.

Vault deposits had held between about $4.48 billion and $4.58 billion from Oct. 29 through Nov. 5, Aavescan's snapshots show. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sky-tvl-falls-15-in-a-week-as-usds-supply-contracts) also reported the weekly decline.

*In our opinion: when an eighth of a savings vault walks out and the rate doesn't twitch, the rate probably wasn't the reason. The useful number now is concentration: if a handful of wallets made Friday's exit, the vault's transaction log will show it before any statement does. Watch whether USDS supply keeps sliding from $5.59 billion this week, because that figure counts dollars leaving the Sky system altogether.*

articles.title: Binance Names Justin Yek CFO Nine Days After $6.3B Hack
articles.excerpt: Co-CEO Yi He said the handover was planned over six months. Yek was vice president of finance at Airwallex; Ng had been CFO since January 2022.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Saturday that finance chief Kaiser Ng is leaving after more than five years, with Justin Yek taking over as CFO. The change comes nine days after hackers took about $6.3 billion from the exchange on Oct. 29, [Reuters reported](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/binance-cfo-kaiser-ng-steps-down-justin-yek-named-new-finance-chief-6533351).

The company tied the move to a plan, not the breach. "Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year," co-CEO Yi He said in a statement carried by Reuters. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/07/binance-cfo-is-leaving-to-pursue-a-new-venture-after-6-3-billion-hack/), citing Bloomberg, reported the same quote.

**Yek comes from a payments company**

Yek was most recently vice president of finance at Airwallex, a payments firm, according to Reuters. Ng has been Binance's CFO since January 2022 and worked at Kraken before that, Reuters said, citing his LinkedIn profile.

Why does the seat matter right now? A chief financial officer runs a company's money: its books, cash, reporting and the reserves that back what it owes. At an exchange, that last part is customer balances. Binance has said it will fully reimburse users hit by the theft, and TechCrunch quoted the company: "These losses will not be passed on to users." Covering a loss that size from company funds is a finance-office job.

**What the statement leaves out**

Neither report gives Ng's last day, says what his new venture is, or explains why the handover was announced now. Binance's statement, as quoted, does not mention the hack.

Binance has said the attack began months earlier with malware hidden in software downloads and fake job offers aimed at its engineers. The FBI has blamed a North Korean hacking group, an allegation Pyongyang has denied, Reuters reported.

*In our opinion: the timing will draw questions, and Binance has answered only one of them: it says the plan predates the breach by six months. The open item is the reimbursement bill, which now lands on a new CFO's desk in his first weeks. The next thing to watch is any Binance update on how much of that reimbursement has been paid, and from which funds.*

articles.title: Treasury Sanctions 8 Canadian Firms Over Alleged Iran Crypto Links
articles.excerpt: OFAC designated eight Ontario and B.C. money services businesses under E.O. 13902. Treasury says they swapped rials and other cash into digital assets for Iran-linked flows.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control on Friday designated eight Canadian money services businesses that it says help move value for Iran by exchanging Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets, according to a [Treasury press release](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0686) and the matching [OFAC SDN update](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261106).

U.S. persons generally may not deal with the firms. Property they hold in the United States is blocked. The action sits under Executive Order 13902, which targets Iran's digital-asset sector among other parts of its economy.

**What OFAC says the firms did**

Treasury alleges the companies, based in Ontario and British Columbia, gave sanctioned Iranian actors a channel to move money abroad. Named firms include Diverse Trade Inc. (Million Exchange), Amin Exchange entities, NIA Nations Currency Ltd., Farah Exchange, CCC Inc., B Galaxy Inc. (Cryptoyal) and Darvish Exchange. OFAC says addresses tied to several of them transacted with sanctioned Iranian exchanges such as Nobitex, Wallex, Ramzinex, Bitpin and Shelbit, and in some cases with addresses linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

A money services business in this context is a firm that changes cash or currencies and, here, often converts those funds into crypto for cross-border transfer. OFAC's list update posts specific TRON addresses for several of the designated entities.

Treasury also says some of the firms handled drug proceeds for Ryan Wedding, a former Olympic snowboarder who was apprehended in January 2026 and who, OFAC alleges, used Canadian exchangers to turn bulk cash into digital assets sent abroad. CBC News reported Friday that it contacted Wedding's lawyer for comment. Public responses from the eight firms were not posted on their sites by midday Saturday ET.

The designations continue Operation Economic Outcast, launched in August, and follow earlier OFAC actions against Iranian exchanges including Nobitex and Shelbit. FinCEN and Canada's FINTRAC coordinated on the package, Treasury said.

Friday's [OFAC update](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261106) lists the eight entities and their TRON addresses on the SDN List. The next check for desks screening counterparties is whether those wallets appear in weekend settlement flows.

articles.title: Binance France Closes Accounts Dec. 31, Fees From Nov. 29
articles.excerpt: A client email sets a Dec. 31 closure after Binance missed MiCA. Idle balances face 0.025% or 10 USDC a month from the Nov. 29 calculation day.
articles.body_md:
Binance France will close every customer account on Dec. 31, 2026, and will start charging monthly fees on Nov. 29 for balances that remain, according to an email to French clients that [Cryptoast published Friday](https://cryptoast.fr/binance-annonce-cloture-comptes-utilisateurs-francais-31-decembre/).

Deposits are already blocked. Withdrawals still work. Accounts emptied before the Nov. 29 "calculation day" pay nothing, the email says.

**How the wind-down works**

The Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation, or MiCA, required EU crypto service providers to hold authorization by June 30, 2026. Binance France did not secure that license. French outlet Cryptoast and Bitcoin.com News both quote the same notice: because of an "orderly cessation of activities," accounts close as of Dec. 31, and assets left behind may be converted, transferred or otherwise handled under Binance's terms.

From Nov. 29, any open Binance France account is charged 0.025% of its balance or 10 USDC, whichever is higher. The first collection is due within three days of Nov. 29; a second is expected after Dec. 24. Fees come from USDC first, then other crypto. If the balance is smaller than the fee, Binance takes what is left.

On a $500 balance, the 10 USDC floor is a 2% hit each month. Only balances above about $40,000 pay the percentage rate instead. Cryptoast says clients can close the account at any time.

Trading for French residents had already ended after the July 1 MiCA transition. The Dec. 31 date ends the withdraw-only window. Neither Binance's global blog nor France's AMF had posted a matching English press release by midday Saturday ET; the client email remains the primary notice.

*In our opinion: the clock for holders is the Nov. 29 calculation day. Accounts emptied before then skip both fee collections. After Dec. 31, leftover assets fall under Binance's terms language; a dated AMF handling schedule has not been posted.*
