articles.title: Intel Sinks 29% on Weak Forecast as Nasdaq Slides Over 2%
articles.excerpt: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15 billion to $16 billion, short of the $17.07 billion analysts expected, and sees the PC slump lasting into 2027.
articles.body_md:
Intel shares fell about 29% Friday morning after the chipmaker forecast weak holiday-quarter sales, helping pull the Nasdaq Composite down 2.3% by 11:06 a.m. ET, [AP reported](https://apnews.com/article/stock-markets-ai-alphabet-oil-16c266731fdf64178f38070af2b42497).

The drop put Intel on track to lose more than $137 billion in market value, [Reuters reported](https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/1030/1597308-intel-quarterly-results/). [CNBC said](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/amazon-intel-earnings-big-tech-ai-spending-concerns.html) the stock was headed for its worst day since 1974.

In its [results release](https://www.intc.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1786/intel-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results), Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share. Analysts expected $17.07 billion and 43 cents, according to LSEG data cited by [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Intel+signals+slower+growth+as+PC+market+remains+under+pressure/27257618.html). The quarter just ended went better: revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, and adjusted earnings of 52 cents beat the 40-cent estimate.

**Why the forecast mattered more**

How it works: a share price is a bet on future profits, so a company's forecast, called guidance, often moves the stock more than the quarter it just reported. Intel's trouble starts with memory. Suppliers have shifted capacity toward the high-bandwidth memory used in AI servers, which raises the cost of building a PC and weighs on demand, Reuters reported.

"We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," finance chief David Zinsner said in the release. Intel also expects an explosion this month at its plant in Israel, which killed two workers, to cost about $600 million in revenue over two quarters, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/intel-intc-q3-earnings-report-2026-.html). Zinsner said Intel does not expect positive cash flow this year.

There is a stronger side to the report. Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, CNBC said, and the stock was up about 150% this year before the results. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Intel expects to announce "a couple of customers" for its contract chipmaking business over the next two quarters.

The selling spread. AMD fell 9.3% and a broad chip index lost 5.7% in early trading, [Reuters reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nasdaq-futures-sink-amazon-intel-114737736.html). Crypto was lower too: bitcoin traded at $77,512 at 12:03 p.m. ET, down 5% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion:* Wall Street is showing little patience for heavy AI-era spending that doesn't turn into cash soon. More than $137 billion of Intel's value was at stake Friday morning, and the rest of the chip group paid part of that bill. The next real test is whether Tan names those outside foundry customers, because that is where the turnaround case lives.

articles.title: TRM Labs Ties $6.36B Binance Hack to North Korea's TraderTraitor
articles.excerpt: The attacker pre-signed 50 Ethereum authorizations and still holds about $2.4 billion in bitcoin and ether that no issuer can freeze, TRM Labs said.
articles.body_md:
Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said it believes with "high confidence" that TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-backed hacking unit, carried out Thursday's theft of about $6.36 billion from Binance.

That puts a name on the largest crypto theft on record. In a [blog post](https://www.trmlabs.com/resources/blog/north-korea-steals-usd-6-36-billion-from-binance-in-the-largest-hack-in-history), TRM said the money left Binance wallets on 10 blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes starting at 4:05 p.m. ET. The FBI [named the same group](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226) for the $1.5 billion Bybit theft in February 2025.

Chainalysis CEO Jonathan Levin also said the attack was likely TraderTraitor's work, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/billions-in-crypto-frozen-in-binance-hack-heres-what-happens-next-.html). Neither is a government finding.

**Signatures prepared in advance**

TRM said preparation began at least 36 hours earlier, funded through Tornado Cash, a service that hides where crypto came from.

How the Ethereum leg worked: EIP-7702, added in Ethereum's May 2025 upgrade, lets an ordinary wallet hand its behavior to a smart contract by signing an authorization. Each wallet keeps a running transaction count, and an authorization only works at the right count. TRM said the attacker had 50 signed authorizations ready for 50 counts in a row, so one would fit no matter how many withdrawals Binance processed. One matched, and a sweeper contract emptied the wallet.

Wallets on nine other chains paid the attacker through ordinary signed transfers. In TRM's view, that points to a compromise of Binance's hot-wallet signing system, which approves payouts. Binance said late Thursday that an engineer's [compromised laptop](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7) may be the cause, and it has not published a full root cause.

**What's frozen and what isn't**

TRM counted about $2.7 billion frozen by Tether, Circle, Ripple, World Liberty Financial and Arbitrum's Security Council. The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4 billion that no issuer can freeze, the firm said.

Bitcoin was at $77,578 at 6 a.m. ET, down 3.2% in 24 hours, and BNB at $702, down 6.2%, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bnb). Black Mint found no public response from North Korea.

*In our opinion:* If the attribution holds, this is TraderTraitor's second record theft in under two years, about four times Bybit's size. The $2.4 billion in bitcoin and ether is the part that matters now, because only tracing and cooperating exchanges can stop it. Watch for the coins to hit bridges and over-the-counter desks, and for Binance's post-mortem to say whether one laptop really reached the signing system.

articles.title: Binance Says Laptop Breach May Be Behind $6.3B Hack, Vows Full Cover
articles.excerpt: Binance puts the hack at about $6.3 billion, names a compromised engineer's laptop as a possible cause and says it will cover all losses as withdrawals stay shut.
articles.body_md:
Binance said at 10:25 PM ET Thursday that a compromised engineer's laptop may be behind a security incident it now puts at about $6.3 billion.

That is the first named cause and the first total from the exchange itself. In an [X post](https://x.com/binance/status/2115993361517891592) linking its [announcement](https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7), Binance said the laptop "allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." It said it found "no evidence of any wallet private key leak" and has revoked the affected address authorisation.

At that size it would be the largest crypto theft on record, the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/business/cryptocurrency/article/3372664/binance-pledges-cover-losses-after-us6-billion-crypto-hack) noted, ahead of the $1.5 billion taken from Bybit in February 2025, which the [FBI tied to North Korea](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226).

How it works: exchanges keep most coins in offline cold storage and a smaller pool in hot wallets that pay out withdrawals automatically. A service container is a walled-off piece of software on a server that does one job, such as sending payout requests. If Binance's early account holds, the attacker never needed the vault keys. Access to the system that asks for withdrawals was enough to move coins out.

Now the money. Binance said about $3 billion has been frozen on-chain with partners, which leaves roughly $3.3 billion not yet frozen by its own numbers. It said it "will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company's funds," that user funds are safe, and that it will publish an updated proof of reserves after the fix.

All deposits and withdrawals are suspended, wider than the partial pause earlier in the evening. Co-founder Yi He [said at 10:32 PM](https://x.com/heyibinance/status/2115995324825370777) withdrawals will reopen once a security scan finishes, with no time given. She also [said](https://x.com/heyibinance/status/2115962957880602653) the Arbitrum Security Council froze about $30.5 million, and Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong [said](https://x.com/brian_armstrong/status/2115976950376210483) Coinbase is blocking sends to compromised wallets.

BNB traded at $717.66 at 11:58 PM ET, down 3.8% over 24 hours, and bitcoin at $78,008, down 2.2%, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bnb).

*In our opinion:* A named cause and a written promise to pay are the two things customers needed tonight, and Binance has now put both on the record. The open question is the $3.3 billion that isn't frozen, which SAFU and company funds would have to fill. Watch for a restart time on withdrawals and the post-mortem, which should show whether one laptop really opened the door.

articles.title: Bank of Japan Says 2% Goal Is Met for First Time Since 2013
articles.excerpt: The Bank of Japan held at 1.25% but called underlying inflation consistent with 2% for the first time since 2013, clearing its own bar for more hikes.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Japan said Friday in Tokyo, late Thursday ET, that underlying inflation is "generally consistent" with its 2% target, a first since it set that goal in 2013.

Until now, the bank had only said inflation was approaching 2%, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/30/boj-inflation-target-rates.html) reported. The bank held its overnight rate at about 1.25%, the highest since 1995, in an 8-1 vote, according to its [policy statement](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030a.pdf). CNBC said board member Hajime Takata dissented in favor of a hike to 1.5%.

The [outlook report](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030b.pdf) raised the fiscal 2027 forecast for consumer prices excluding fresh food to 2.6% from 2.4%, and said price risks are "skewed to the upside" as firms lean more toward raising wages and prices. The other side: experts told CNBC that energy subsidies are holding headline price numbers down, so part of the pressure is masked.

The bank also sped up its exit from the stock market. Starting January 2027, it will sell its exchange-traded funds at about 860 billion yen a year at book value, up from 330 billion, per its [ETF decision](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmdeci/mpr_2026/k261030c.pdf). That cuts the time to finish selling from about 112 years to about 43. Brisk, by central bank standards.

How it works: "underlying" inflation strips out jumpy items like fresh food and energy, so it shows whether price rises are spreading through wages and services. Saying it has reached 2% is the test the bank set for itself before raising rates further. Why crypto readers care: for years, near-zero Japanese rates made the yen a cheap currency to borrow and invest elsewhere. Higher Japanese rates make that trade costlier, and unwinding it can pull money out of risk assets, crypto included.

All 16 economists in a CNBC survey expect the bank to set up a hike in December or January.

*In our opinion:* Thirteen years of "approaching" just became "consistent," and that one word change is the bank clearing its own bar for more hikes. The stake for crypto is the cheap-yen funding that has backed risk trades worldwide for years. Watch the December meeting and the yen, because a fast move in either can spill into crypto.

articles.title: Binance Pauses Some Withdrawals as $2.54B Frozen After Alleged Multi-Billion Hack
articles.excerpt: Trackers allege $5.7B to $5.8B was taken, which Binance hasn't confirmed. Tether and Circle froze more than 2.3 billion in stablecoins.
articles.body_md:
Binance has paused withdrawals on multiple networks while it investigates what security firms and trackers allege is a multi-billion-dollar hack of its hot wallets. At 7:22 p.m. ET Thursday, the exchange [said](https://x.com/binance/status/2115947325617299903) the "current verified total frozen is $2.54 billion" and that its teams are working closely with law enforcement.

Binance has not called the event a hack, given a loss figure or said who is behind it. At 6:15 p.m. it [said](https://x.com/binance/status/2115930656589119995) withdrawals "will resume as soon as the security issue is fully resolved" and that "user funds remain safe." A spokesperson called the pause a "precautionary measure," [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/29/binance-pauses-withdrawals-as-hackers-suspected-of-stealing-billions-in-crypto/).

**What the trackers allege**

The outflows began about 4:24 p.m. ET, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/binance-says-user-funds-are-completely-safe-after-3-5-billion-drains-from-its-hot-wallets/). PeckShieldAlert [posted](https://x.com/PeckShieldAlert/status/2115917332786851967) "Confirmed hack" at 5:22 p.m. At 7:27 p.m., tracker Lookonchain [alleged](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2115948651554157043) that more than $5.8 billion was stolen and is being sold for other tokens. Arkham data put the total near $5.7 billion, per a post [Arkham shared](https://x.com/arkham/status/2115952424171061288). Binance has not confirmed either number.

**How a stablecoin freeze works**

USDT and USDC are tokens whose issuers can block a wallet address. Once an address is frozen, the tokens in it can't be sent or swapped, but they aren't returned yet. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino [said](https://x.com/paoloardoino/status/2115918000373346709) the company froze more than 1.567 billion USDT. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire [said](https://x.com/jerallaire/status/2115916207463481846) Circle froze more than 800 million USDC "in coordination with law enforcement." Coins like ether have no issuer, so they can't be frozen this way.

**Who says they will pay**

Founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs Binance, [wrote](https://x.com/cz_binance/status/2115915423174853077) that it "does look like a hack." At 6:23 p.m. he [replied](https://x.com/cz_binance/status/2115932500006756686) to a post estimating the net loss near $1 billion: "Loss might be a bit higher than that, but will cover." For scale, the FBI [tied](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226) a $1.5 billion theft from Bybit in February 2025 to North Korea.

BNB traded near $703 at 7:45 p.m. ET, down 7.3% in 24 hours, and bitcoin near $78,460, down 3.4%, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: The $2.54 billion frozen is the only figure Binance itself stands behind, and the tracker totals are more than twice that. If those totals hold, the alleged theft would be nearly four times the size of Bybit's. Until withdrawals resume, users on the paused networks can't move funds off the exchange. Watch for Binance's own loss figure, a named cause and a date for withdrawals to restart.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Drops 3% to $78,177 as Billions Leave Binance Hot Wallets
articles.excerpt: $627.7 million in bets were force-closed in an hour, 97% of them longs. BNB fell about 9%, three times bitcoin's drop.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell about 3% in 45 minutes Thursday, from near $80,740 at 3:55 p.m. ET to a low of $78,177 at 4:45 p.m. on Coinbase, as billions of dollars flowed out of Binance hot wallets. It traded near $79,100 at 6:25 p.m., down 2.5% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

**The timeline**

The first transfers out of a wallet Etherscan labels Binance 14 landed at 4:24 p.m. ET, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/binance-says-user-funds-are-completely-safe-after-3-5-billion-drains-from-its-hot-wallets/). The sharpest bitcoin candles printed in the 20 minutes after that, Coinbase price data show. Binance said at 5:29 p.m. that ["user funds are completely safe."](https://x.com/binance/status/2115918888429133902) Bitcoin had already slipped about 0.5% in the 4 p.m. candle, before the transfers, so not all of the drop lines up.

**Update, 7:50 p.m. ET:** Binance has since [paused withdrawals](https://x.com/binance/status/2115930656589119995) on multiple networks, [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/29/binance-pauses-withdrawals-as-hackers-suspected-of-stealing-billions-in-crypto/). It [says](https://x.com/binance/status/2115947325617299903) $2.54 billion is frozen, with law enforcement helping. Trackers [Lookonchain](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2115948651554157043) and [Arkham](https://x.com/arkham/status/2115952424171061288) allege $5.7 billion to $5.8 billion was taken. Binance has not confirmed a loss or called it a hack.

**How a small drop turned into a fast one**

Many traders borrow to make bigger bets on futures. If the price moves far enough against them, the exchange sells their position by force. That is a liquidation, and each forced sale can push the price lower and trip the next one. Coinglass data counted $627.7 million in liquidations in one hour, 97% of it on bets that prices would rise, [BeInCrypto reported](https://beincrypto.com/crypto-liquidations-binance-hack-fears/). The largest was an $11.09 million bitcoin long on Binance at $79,254, which [SwoleCharts](https://swolecharts.com/liquidations/daily/2026-10-29) also logged at 4:42 p.m. ET.

**Who took the biggest hit**

BNB, Binance's own token, fell about 9% from 4 p.m. to its low near $678, OKX data show. Ether fell about 4.4% to near $2,233. Tether [said](https://x.com/paoloardoino/status/2115918000373346709) it froze more than 1.567 billion USDT, and Circle froze about 823 million USDC, Unchained reported.

The market was soft before the outflows. Bitcoin dipped under $80,000 late Wednesday after the Fed held rates, and options on about $10.8 billion of bitcoin expire Friday at 4 a.m. ET on Deribit.

*In our opinion: the clock points at Binance. The selling started within minutes of the outflows, and the coin most tied to Binance fell three times as hard as bitcoin. The macro news set a weak floor, but it didn't light the fuse. Watch for Binance's next official update, and for whether bitcoin holds $78,000 through Friday's 4 a.m. expiry.*

articles.title: Binance Probes Billions in Hot-Wallet Outflows, Says Funds Are Safe
articles.excerpt: Billions left Binance hot wallets Thursday. Tether froze 1.567B USDT, CZ said it looks like a hack, and Binance says user funds are safe.
articles.body_md:
Binance said Thursday its security teams are "actively investigating" after wallets tied to the exchange sent billions of dollars in crypto to a single new address, starting around 4:24 p.m. ET.

The exchange first said at 5:16 p.m. that it had "not confirmed any impact to user funds." Thirteen minutes later it [edited that post](https://x.com/binance/status/2115918888429133902) to say "User funds are completely safe." It has not called the event a hack.

**Update, 7:50 p.m. ET:** Binance has since [paused withdrawals](https://x.com/binance/status/2115930656589119995) on multiple networks, [TechCrunch reported](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/29/binance-pauses-withdrawals-as-hackers-suspected-of-stealing-billions-in-crypto/). It [says](https://x.com/binance/status/2115947325617299903) $2.54 billion is frozen, with law enforcement helping. Trackers [Lookonchain](https://x.com/lookonchain/status/2115948651554157043) and [Arkham](https://x.com/arkham/status/2115952424171061288) allege $5.7 billion to $5.8 billion was taken. Binance has not confirmed a loss or called it a hack.

**What moved**

Unchained counted about $3.52 billion leaving on Ethereum alone between 4:24 and 5:04 p.m. ET, including 197,170 ETH, 1.68 billion USDT and 823 million USDC, [per its report](https://unchainedcrypto.com/binance-says-user-funds-are-completely-safe-after-3-5-billion-drains-from-its-hot-wallets/). That count leaves out other chains, so the total may be higher. Security firm Blockaid [said](https://x.com/blockaid_/status/2115914335512150480) the transfers "look consistent with unauthorized movement" but that it "cannot yet rule out an internal treasury or operational sweep."

**How it appears to work**

A hot wallet is the internet-connected account an exchange uses to pay out withdrawals. Unchained reported that an address partly funded through the mixer Tornado Cash set up an EIP-7702 delegation on one of those wallets at 4:20 p.m. That Ethereum feature lets an ordinary wallet run a smart contract's code. Whoever controls the code can move the funds. How the delegation was signed is not yet known.

**Freezes and pledges**

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino [said](https://x.com/paoloardoino/status/2115918000373346709) the company froze more than 1.567 billion USDT "related to a potential Binance exchange hack." Former CEO Changpeng Zhao [wrote](https://x.com/cz_binance/status/2115915423174853077) that it "does look like a hack" and that, as a shareholder, he expects user funds "will be fully covered." The outflows were still running at 5:44 p.m., Unchained said.

For scale, the FBI [tied a $1.5 billion theft](https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2025/PSA250226) from Bybit in February 2025 to North Korea. No one has named a culprit here. BNB traded near $707 at 6:01 p.m. ET, down 6.6% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: The freezes bought time, but frozen tokens are not returned tokens. Binance has said funds are safe without saying what happened. The next statement needs a cause, a final number and who pays.*

articles.title: Coinbase Posts $719M Q3 Profit, Mostly From Crypto It Kept
articles.excerpt: Coinbase made $719 million in Q3, but $715 million was a paper gain on its own crypto. Adjusted profit was $77.7 million.
articles.body_md:
Coinbase earned $719 million in the third quarter, its first profit in three quarters, the exchange [reported Thursday](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1679788/000167978826000121/q326earningsdeck_vsec.htm). Almost all of it came from coins it didn't sell.

About $715 million of that profit was a paper gain on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment. Strip that out, along with other investment gains, and adjusted net income was $77.7 million. Analysts had expected a loss of 15 cents a share, per Zacks data [cited by Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/382188/coinbase-beats-719-million-q3-profit-crypto-gains). Coinbase posted $2.51 per diluted share.

**How the paper gain works**

Accounting rules make Coinbase mark its own crypto to market each quarter. When prices rise between June 30 and Sept. 30, the gain lands in net income even though nothing was sold. When prices fall, it runs the other way. Ask the first quarter: the swing cost Coinbase $482 million in the first quarter.

**The business underneath**

Trading fees keep shrinking.

- Total revenue was $1.22 billion, flat from the second quarter and down 35% from a year ago.
- Trading revenue slipped 1% to $590 million. Crypto volatility hit multi-year lows, the company said.
- Subscription and services revenue rose 3% to $570 million, 49% of the total. Stablecoin revenue was $307 million.
- Prediction markets passed $200 million in annualized revenue.

Coinbase also trimmed its 2026 adjusted expense outlook by $100 million at the midpoint, to $4.15 billion to $4.3 billion. Shares closed at $160.59 before the release and barely moved after hours, Decrypt reported.

*In our opinion: The profit is real, but most of it was the market's doing. The steadier story is stablecoin interest and prediction markets doing the work trading fees used to. Watch whether that holds if rates fall.*

articles.title: ECB Holds Rates at 2.5% as Lagarde Sets Feb. 7 Exit Date
articles.excerpt: Euro-area inflation hit 3.8% in September, and money markets now see about a 67% chance of a December hike, per LSEG data cited by CNBC.
articles.body_md:
The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.50% on Thursday, hours after President Christine Lagarde told policymakers she will step down on Feb. 7, 2027.

The hold comes with euro-area inflation at 3.8% in September, up from 3.2% in August, and energy inflation at 18.9%, [the ECB's press conference statement](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/press_conference/monetary-policy-statement/2026/html/ecb.is261029~5c5ffe99e5.en.html) shows. The dollar extended gains against the euro after the decision, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/european-central-bank-interest-rates.html).

**Policymakers debated a hike**

Lagarde told reporters that "the Governing Council debated whether a hike was appropriate" before voting unanimously to hold, according to CNBC. The bank's own release says it is "not pre-committing to a particular rate path." Its other two rates stay at 2.65% and 2.90%.

Money markets priced about a 67% chance of a December hike after the announcement, CNBC reported, citing LSEG data. Deutsche Bank economist Mark Wall expects one more increase, to 2.75%, in December. UBS's Dean Turner called Thursday's move "a hawkish pause rather than the end of the tightening cycle."

**The European Council picks her successor**

The next president will be appointed by the European Council under Article 283 of the EU treaty, [the ECB said](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr261029~abbb6dc64b.en.html). Its release gives no reason for the timing and names no candidates.

Bitcoin was near $81,630 at 11:56 a.m. ET, up 1.5% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: December now carries two stories, a possible hike and a president with about two months left. The figure to check first is November's euro-area inflation reading.*

articles.title: US Economy Grows 3.4% as September PCE Inflation Hits 3.6%
articles.excerpt: Prices rose 0.5% in September alone, up from 0.3% in August, a day after the Fed held rates at 3.75%-4%. Next GDP revision: Nov. 25.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, the Bureau of Economic Analysis said Thursday, while its September price gauge showed inflation running at 3.6% from a year earlier.

That pairing reached the Fed one day after it held its benchmark rate at 3.75%-4%. The PCE price index is the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, and it sits well above the 2% target. Rates matter to crypto because Treasury bills pay interest and bitcoin doesn't.

**Growth beat the forecast**

- GDP rose 3.4%, up from 2.2% in the second quarter, [BEA's advance estimate](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-advance-estimate-3rd-quarter-2026) shows. Economists had expected 3.1%, per the Dow Jones consensus [cited by CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/pce-inflation-report-september-2026-.html).
- Consumer spending plus private fixed investment rose 4.9%, from 4.6%.
- Personal income rose 0.2% in September.

**Prices sped up for the month**

The PCE index rose 0.5% in September after 0.3% in August, [BEA's income report](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-september-2026) shows. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year. The annual headline figure came in 0.1 percentage point below the consensus, and core matched it, CNBC reported.

The quarter looks cooler. Over July through September, PCE prices rose at a 2.1% annual pace, down from 5.0% in the second quarter.

Next on the calendar: BEA's second GDP estimate, due Nov. 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Bitcoin was near $81,630 at 11:56 a.m. ET, up 1.5% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: Thursday mailed the Fed faster growth and faster monthly price gains in the same envelope. The calmer 2.1% quarterly pace is the counterweight.*

articles.title: Utah Files 14 Criminal Charges Against Kalshi and Its Co-Founders
articles.excerpt: An undercover state investigator placed 12 sports bets on Kalshi in 11 days. Kalshi called the felony case "a crazy overreach."
articles.body_md:
Utah filed 14 criminal charges on Wednesday against Kalshi and its co-founders, CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara, accusing them of illegally promoting gambling in the state.

The case moves the state's fight with the prediction market from civil court to criminal court. Kalshi said it will fight the charges.

**Twelve bets from an undercover account**

The [charging document](https://attorneygeneral.utah.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Utah-v.-Kalshi.pdf) lists one second-degree felony count of pattern of unlawful activity, 12 third-degree felony counts of online gambling promotion and one misdemeanor.

It says an attorney general's investigator opened an account with Utah details on Sept. 13 and placed 12 sports wagers in 11 days. One was a $5 bet on a Utah-Utah State football spread that paid $4.13, the [Deseret News](https://www.deseret.com/sports/2026/10/28/utah-files-criminal-charges-kalshi-illegal-gambling-promotion-cftc-sues-utah-block-laws/) reported. Kalshi took fees of 3 to 78 cents per trade, the charges allege.

The bigger dollar figure sits in Utah's separate civil suit. It alleges Kalshi made between $30.5 million and $61.1 million from Utah accounts from February through Oct. 19, the Deseret News reported.

**Both sides dig in**

"Calling it a 'prediction market' doesn't change what it is," Attorney General Derek Brown said in a statement to [FOX 13](https://www.fox13now.com/news/politics/utah-levels-criminal-charges-against-kalshi-and-some-of-its-executives).

A Kalshi spokesperson called the charges "a crazy overreach" and said "Utah is clearly playing politics," adding that the company expects to win in court "just like we did in Arizona," FOX 13 reported. A federal judge blocked Arizona's prosecution of Kalshi.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah on Monday, arguing federal law covers event contracts and they "are not gambling," [KSL](https://www.ksl.com/article/51642075/feds-sue-utah-over-attempt-to-ban-kalshi-ag-files-criminal-charges-in-response) reported. In August, a federal judge in Utah ruled the other way on Kalshi's own suit. An appeal is pending.

The co-founders were issued summonses to appear in court. The charges are allegations and have not been proven in court.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

sources.name: Utah Attorney General, criminal information in State of Utah v. KalshiEX LLC

articles.title: ADGM Gives Crypto Miners License Code 7230 in Abu Dhabi
articles.excerpt: Miners file their on-chain reward addresses with the registrar, and custodial staking may need a separate financial permit.
articles.body_md:
Abu Dhabi's financial free zone now has a rulebook for crypto miners. ADGM's Registration Authority said Wednesday that miners get their own commercial license, code 7230, and that mining is not a regulated financial service.

That puts miners under the company registrar. The financial regulator steps in only when client assets are involved.

**One code for every consensus method**

Operators need the commercial license to mine in or from the zone, the [announcement](https://www.adgm.com/media/announcements/adgm-becomes-the-regions-first-international-financial-centre-to-publish-dedicated-crypto-mining-guidance) says. The rules apply to proof-of-work, proof-of-stake and future consensus methods alike.

Mining for your own account is in. Holding other people's coins is a different matter. The [guidance](https://assets.adgm.com/download/assets/ADGM+Registration+Authority+-+Guidance+on+Crypto+Mining+Activities.pdf/07dfa300be3711f1b38dd6c93cb25020) says pooled staking, custodial delegation or managing third-party assets may also need a permission from the Financial Services Regulatory Authority. Non-custodial infrastructure that never touches client assets does not, for now.

**What miners hand over**

Licensees must disclose their corporate structure and ultimate beneficial owners. They also file their on-chain reward addresses, which the registrar keeps confidential. Supervision scales with the size and risk of each operation, and firms can run global mining from an ADGM headquarters.

**Phase one of two**

The guidance followed an eight-week public consultation earlier this year, the state-run [WAM](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c2yy6ib-adgm-becomes-regions-first-international-financial) news service reported. A second phase will build a full regulatory framework, with another market consultation "in due course."

"With this Guidance, ADGM is open to responsible crypto mining," said Rashed Al Blooshi, the registration authority's CEO.

*In our opinion: the reward-address rule is the sleeper here. Hashrate is easy to promise on a slide, but a wallet address tends to tell the truth.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

sources.name: ADGM Registration Authority, Guidance on Crypto Mining Activities (PDF)

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Fixes Bug That Let Peers Take Down Windows, Mac Nodes
articles.excerpt: Linux nodes weren't exposed to the node shutdown bug. A separate low-severity flaw still affects 32-bit systems and FAT32 drives after the update.
articles.body_md:
Any connected peer was able to take down a Bitcoin node running on Windows, macOS or BSD, Bitcoin Core developers disclosed Wednesday, Oct. 28. Fixes shipped this week in versions 29.5, 30.4, 31.2 and 32.1.

It was one of three bugs published that day. Linux nodes aren't affected by this one.

**A paused peer could keep sending**

Bitcoin Core normally stops reading from a peer once that peer's data piles up past a limit. On non-Linux systems, a peer was able to slip past that pause by sending TCP "urgent" data, so the node kept queuing data until it ran out of memory. The project rates it medium severity and says a malicious peer "can trivially crash any Windows, macOS or BSD node it is connected to."

The second medium-severity bug let a peer that claimed not to support BIP 31 pings (an older connection check) grow a node's memory by up to 2MB an hour per inbound peer, or 5MB per outbound peer. Nodes running `-blocksonly` are much less exposed.

**One flaw outlives the patch**

The third bug, rated low, lets a miner corrupt the undo files nodes use to roll back blocks during a reorganization. On 64-bit machines the project calls it impractical: an attacker would need to mine roughly a month of the whole network's blocks. Nodes on 32-bit systems or storing blocks on FAT32 drives remain affected.

Two of the three bugs were first flagged by an automated scan using a large language model, part of Elias Rohrer's Project Loupe at Spiral, and validated by developer Gregory Sanders.

*In our opinion: the date that stands out is Oct. 23. That's when the scan flagged the Windows and Mac bug, and patched releases were out four days later.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Slips Under $80,000 Ahead of Friday's Options Expiry
articles.excerpt: Options on about 135,600 BTC expire Friday on Deribit, roughly $10.8 billion, with calls outnumbering puts nearly 2 to 1.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin fell below $80,000 late Wednesday and was near $79,700 at 12:05 a.m. ET Thursday, down 1.6% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko. Ether was down 2.3% at about $2,300.

The round number has some history this fall. CoinGecko's daily price series last had bitcoin under $80,000 on Sept. 17, near $76,400.

**Friday's expiry edges out Christmas**

On Deribit, options on about 135,600 BTC expire Friday, Oct. 30, at 8 a.m. UTC (4 a.m. ET), the exchange's data showed at midnight ET. That's roughly $10.8 billion. The Dec. 25 expiry is almost as big, smaller by fewer than 300 BTC.

An option is the right to buy (a call) or sell (a put) at a set price by a set date. Friday's batch holds about 88,900 BTC in calls and 46,700 in puts. By Black Mint's calculation from Deribit's open interest, the strike where those contracts would pay out the least is $78,000.

**Not all the flows went one way**

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $137.3 million on Wednesday, Farside Investors data show. That same day, the Federal Reserve held rates at 3.75% to 4%, with two officials voting for a hike.

Sentiment barely moved. The crypto Fear & Greed Index read 51, labeled "neutral," at midnight.

*In our opinion: a 1.6% slip only makes noise because of the zeros. The number worth chasing settles Friday at 4 a.m. ET.*

articles.title: Bessent Tells Swell That Stablecoins Will Help Fund the Treasury
articles.excerpt: With the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, Bessent said regulators can "convene" to set crypto rules. Treasury hasn't posted a transcript of the Oct. 27 talk.
articles.body_md:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Ripple's Swell conference on Tuesday, Oct. 27, that dollar stablecoins are "going to be an important source of funding for the Treasury."

More than 90% of stablecoins are pegged to the dollar, Bessent said, and issuers back them largely with government debt, [American Banker](https://www.americanbanker.com/news/bessent-stablecoins-will-help-ensure-dollar-dominance) reported. Dollar stablecoins totaled nearly $280 billion at the end of 2025, a [Brookings paper](https://www.brookings.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Liang-Dudley-GENIUS-Act.pdf) shows.

He sat on stage with Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse, who called it "an honor" on [X](https://x.com/bgarlinghouse/status/2115216477045624862). Treasury hadn't posted a transcript or readout by 9 p.m. ET Wednesday, its [press page](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases) shows.

## Stablecoins as the answer to CBDCs

He called stablecoins "backed by U.S. regulation" but issued by private firms "the answer to central bank digital currencies," American Banker reported.

He gave no dollar figure or date.

## Agencies step in after CLARITY stalled

With no market-structure law, Bessent said regulators could "convene" to set crypto rules, American Banker reported. [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/regulation-and-legal/bessent-clarity-act-plan-b-ripple-swell/) reported he named the SEC and CFTC and called the bill's failure a disappointment. Citing attendees, it said he wants regulators to set "guardrails" against debanking crypto firms.

The bill fell short of the 60 Senate votes needed to advance on Sept. 15, [Senate records](https://www.dailypress.senate.gov/tuesday-september-15-2026/) show. Sen. Thom Tillis voted no so he could bring it back, [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/politics-news/us-senate-to-vote-on-advancing-landmark-crypto-bill-4901156) reported.

## The case against a Treasury windfall

Nellie Liang and William Dudley wrote that the net effect on federal debt costs is "likely to be negligible." New stablecoin buying may displace banks and money funds that already hold bills, they said. Dudley sits on Coinbase's advisory council, the Brookings paper discloses.

*In our opinion: the pitch gets a test date. The GENIUS Act takes effect Jan. 18, 2027, per the OCC's [final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/23/2026-21706/implementing-the-guiding-and-establishing-national-innovation-for-us-stablecoins-act-for-the), and issuer reserve reports will show how many bills they buy.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

sources.name: Brookings, Liang and Dudley, "Next Steps for GENIUS" (March 2026)
Federal Register, OCC final GENIUS Act rule

articles.title: Fed Holds Rates at 3.75%-4% as Cook and Hammack Vote for a Hike
articles.excerpt: The 10-2 vote keeps the range set by September's hike. The Fed said inflation "remains elevated" and gave no date for its next move.
articles.body_md:
The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on Wednesday, Oct. 28, in a 10-2 vote, and said inflation "remains elevated."

Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented. Both wanted a quarter-point hike, the Fed's statement says. It was Cook's first dissent since she joined the Fed in 2022, CNBC reported.

For crypto holders, the Fed rate sets the price of cash. The higher it sits, the more an asset with no yield, like bitcoin, has to compete with interest-paying bills and deposits.

## The range stays where September put it

The Fed raised rates a quarter point in September and has held since, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/28/fed-interest-rate-decision-october-2026.html) and [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Fed+holds+rates+steady+as+it+awaits+accumulation+of+more+information/27248284.html). This time the statement called growth "expanding at a strong pace" and said more information would help the committee pick its next step. It gave no date for one.

The Fed's implementation note keeps interest on reserve balances at 3.90%, effective Oct. 29.

Neither the statement nor the note changes margin requirements.

## Futures still lean toward a December hike

Traders had priced less than a 10% chance of a hike at this meeting, CNBC reported, citing CME Group's FedWatch tool. Investors still expect hikes starting in December, Reuters reported. The next meeting is Dec. 8-9, with new projections.

Chair Kevin Warsh also said one of the eight meetings in 2027 will cover strategy only, with no rate vote and no statement, according to CNBC and [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/live/fed-meeting-live-updates-federal-reserve-october-meeting-kevin-warsh-161129201.html).

Bitcoin moved little: about $80,800 at 2 p.m. ET and $80,900 at 2:57 p.m., up 0.4% over 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the hold was the expected part. Two votes for a hike, one of them a first, are what to remember when the Fed meets again Dec. 8-9.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: US Sanctions 11 Targets in North Korea IT Worker Crypto Networks
articles.excerpt: Treasury says a Russian national converted about $3.5 million in crypto for a sanctioned North Korean IT firm as it names 10 people and one entity.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Treasury sanctioned 10 people and one entity on Wednesday, Oct. 28, accusing them of moving crypto and other funds for North Korea's IT worker schemes.

Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) said the networks rely on fraudulent documents, stolen identities and made-up personas to land jobs at U.S. and allied companies, and that North Korea's government takes most of the workers' wages to fund its weapons programs. Those schemes bring in hundreds of millions of dollars, Treasury said.

## The crypto trail

OFAC put figures on the crypto side. It said Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov exchanged and converted about $3.5 million in crypto for Alis, a North Korean IT company. It said Russian intermediary Vitold Viktorovich Obertas made nearly $2 million in crypto conversions for North Korean officials since January 2025, and that Kim Ki Hyok moved nearly $500,000 in crypto for a Russia-based IT worker delegation.

The entity, the First Financial and Technical Development Center, is a North Korea-controlled group in Russia whose workers generated more than $750,000, Treasury said.

## What the designation does

Property of those named that is in the U.S. or held by U.S. persons is now blocked, and U.S. persons are generally barred from dealing with them. OFAC can impose civil penalties on a strict liability basis, so a firm can be fined even if it did not know who it was dealing with.

The action builds on OFAC's March 12 designation of a separate network, and Treasury said Australia and the EU also designated North Korea-linked targets this month. Treasury's release did not include responses from those named. [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMinwFBVV95cUxNWUtIYXNSS25velBzRjB0ZGpaYWtLdDhVb3VVeUprZUkxeEVBWUlMdC0wc2gyUU5UR3FWOHozOWdxRThDNlVHRC1aVFBzVGJsZThtLUZWMmEza3QtU0Y4c0VxQlptYjlVbEtuV2NEQ1dzeHVNMjR0RUlCX2Rla0NhbkFFdmlxOFVQbTBfZUpEWXRjQno2Q3VEblB5Q2RDcHM?oc=5) also reported the sanctions.

*In our opinion: Naming the people who convert the coins goes after the cash-out step, and that is where these schemes leave the clearest trail.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Bank of Canada Hikes to 2.5% and Leaves the Door Open to More
articles.excerpt: Canada's central bank raised rates 25 basis points on energy-driven inflation and said another increase may be needed, but it will proceed carefully.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.5% on Wednesday, Oct. 28, and said it may need to go higher.

The move lifts the Bank Rate to 2.75% and the deposit rate to 2.45%, according to the central bank's release. Governing Council said it acted "to reduce the risk that continuing high energy prices spread broadly to the prices of other goods and services."

## Why the bank moved

CPI inflation has run around 3% since April and should reach about 3½% by year-end, the bank said. It now expects inflation to average 3% in 2027, a percentage point above its July projection, before easing to 2% by mid-2028. It pointed to higher-for-longer energy prices tied to the Middle East conflict, now in its eighth month, and to companies passing more costs on to customers.

The other side of the ledger is softer. Inflation excluding gasoline was 2.2% in September, core measures sit near 2%, and unemployment is around 6½%. The bank forecasts growth of 1% this year and 2% in 2027 and 2028.

## What comes next

"There could be a need to increase the policy rate further, but given uncertainties, Governing Council agreed to proceed carefully," the bank said. [Reuters](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitAFBVV95cUxOQUNfMFh2VXFuRUpyWjNldzQ4dmZROU5kNjhfUlNoXzd1UXNWV0NiTXJiclpmYUlnS1dFUXJ0QkVPVno1VkJxaEpOUDc5Qk5PS2ZBR1NUbE5RSU5ja2FRQmVpd1VZZWhmdjl6dzRFTE9hNGJvWHNCc2VFN2NFQlNvYzNtdjYwWnVoNmdIZUdMRkZBbHY2OTJ1OEpvMFlRYkRHY2ZVZmZKM2RUdU9IckpCMzV2Wm4?oc=5) reported the decision the same way, as leaving another hike possible. The next rate announcement is Dec. 9.

The decision lands hours before the Federal Reserve's 2 p.m. ET announcement. Bitcoin traded at $80,440 at 11:59 a.m. ET, down 0.1% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: The hike made the headline, but the scoop is in the fine print, where "proceed carefully" is central-bank speak for "don't count on a quiet December."*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

sources.name: Bank of Canada, Oct. 28 rate announcement

articles.title: Bithumb Says Staff Data Leaked in Breach, Still Checking Customer Data
articles.excerpt: South Korea's FSC held an emergency meeting Wednesday and started on-site checks. No leak of wallet addresses has been confirmed, the regulator said.
articles.body_md:
An outsider broke into an internal mobile system Bithumb staff use for work and messaging, and personal data leaked, the exchange said Oct. 28.

Whether customer data was taken is still being checked, South Korea's Financial Services Commission said. Data on employees of Bithumb, its subsidiaries and partner firms leaked, Bithumb told the FSC at an emergency meeting on Oct. 28, according to the regulator's statement. Neither the FSC nor Bithumb has said what kinds of employee data were exposed.

## What was and wasn't hit

The breached system is not a core crypto trading system, Bithumb reported to the FSC. So far, no leak of information that could be used for fraudulent payments or crypto transfers, such as wallet addresses, has been confirmed, the FSC said.

Bithumb said it spotted the access on Oct. 27 and reported it that day to the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Personal Information Protection Commission, DigitalToday reported. "This is a system used only by employees and is separated from the exchange's network," a Bithumb official told Yonhap Infomax.

Yonhap, citing an unnamed industry source, reported that some customer information had leaked. Bithumb has not confirmed that. The number of people affected and how the intruder got in are still unknown.

## Brokers and fund managers hit too

Daishin Securities said data on 38,490 customers leaked, Yonhap reported. The FSC said Mirae Asset Life and Mirae Asset Global Investments had also recently reported incidents.

The FSC, the Financial Supervisory Service and the Financial Security Institute began on-site checks. If customers suffer losses, the FSC said, it will supervise steps such as full compensation.

Bithumb has told employees and could send customers a notice if a member-data leak is confirmed, DigitalToday reported.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Datavault AI Says It Can't Withdraw Its Bitcoin, Will Restate Results
articles.excerpt: A June withdrawal from Biconomy still hasn't gone through. The fix cuts reported assets by up to $92.2 million, and the shares fell about 50%.
articles.body_md:
Datavault AI has been unable to withdraw bitcoin from the exchange Biconomy since June and will restate results, cutting reported assets by up to $92.2 million, an SEC filing on Monday shows.

Four sets of statements "should no longer be relied upon," the company said. The shares fell 49.6% on Tuesday to about 6.7 cents, from 13.3 cents, TokenPost reported. The expected cut is $92.2 million as of Dec. 31, 2025, and $49 million as of June 30, 2026.

## How the bitcoin got there

In September 2025, Scilex Holding agreed to buy Datavault stock for $150 million, paid in bitcoin (about 1,328 BTC), the filing says.

Scilex then credited 1,309.04 BTC to Datavault's Biconomy account off-chain: balances changed on the exchange's books, and nothing moved on the blockchain. Between September 2025 and January 2026, Datavault sold 491.431 of those BTC back to Scilex for about $40.5 million in cash.

In June, Datavault asked to move bitcoin to an outside account. It still hasn't happened. The filing doesn't say how much or why.

## The coins become an IOU from Scilex

Datavault's audit committee decided on Oct. 20 that the bitcoin never qualified as a company digital asset. It will be booked as a subscription receivable, money Scilex owes for the shares, reducing stockholders' equity.

Because collecting from Scilex is uncertain, management is reassessing its going-concern evaluation, the filing says. No date is set for the corrected filings.

Black Mint found no public comment from Biconomy on the filing on its X account or in news coverage by 6:05 a.m. ET Wednesday.

*In our opinion:* An exchange balance is a promise, and the coins are only yours once they can leave. Next to check: whether the restated filings say any of it ever reached a wallet Datavault controls.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Australia's Inflation Climbs to 4.3%, Above Forecast, Before RBA Vote
articles.excerpt: September CPI beat the 4.2% forecast as fuel and power costs jumped. The RBA, already at 4.60% after a September hike, meets Nov. 2-3.
articles.body_md:
Australia's annual inflation rate rose to 4.3% in September from 4.0% in August, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said at 11:30 a.m. Sydney time Wednesday (8:30 p.m. ET Tuesday). The consensus forecast was 4.2%, according to FXStreet.

Prices rose 0.8% in the month before seasonal adjustment, against a 0.7% forecast and 0.4% in August, FXStreet's tally of the release shows.

## Where the pressure came from

Transport led the climb, up 8.7% from a year earlier and 3.0% in September alone, the ABS said. Housing costs rose 5.2%, driven by a 12.8% jump in electricity prices, while rents rose 3.6%. So the two bills that are hardest to skip, the fuel tank and the power meter, did most of the work.

The trimmed mean, a core gauge that strips out the biggest price swings, rose to 3.6% from a revised 3.5%. That is above the Reserve Bank of Australia's 2% to 3% target band.

## The rate picture

The RBA lifted its cash rate target to 4.60% on Sept. 30, its fourth increase this year, the central bank's records show. Its Monetary Policy Board next meets Nov. 2-3. FXStreet said the print added to bets on a November hike, and the Australian dollar rose to about $0.705, its highest since Sept. 23.

Crypto barely moved on the release. Bitcoin traded near $81,020 at midnight ET, up 1.7% in 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. Traders now turn to the U.S. Federal Reserve's two-day meeting, FXStreet noted.

*In our opinion:* The number that matters is Nov. 3, when the RBA shows whether a hotter September changes its plan. A fifth hike this year would be the clearest sign yet that the RBA expects this inflation to stick around.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

sources.name: Reserve Bank of Australia, cash rate
Reserve Bank of Australia, meeting schedule

articles.title: Coinbase Says Vendor Amplitude Exposed Some Customer Contact Data
articles.excerpt: Coinbase says its own systems weren't breached and funds weren't touched, but it hasn't said how many users were hit or which fields leaked.
articles.body_md:
Coinbase said late Tuesday that a security incident at Amplitude, an analytics vendor it uses, exposed contact data for "a small subset" of its customers. The exchange posted the statement on its Coinbase Support account on X at 10:49 p.m. ET.

"Coinbase has not had a data breach," the company wrote. It said it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its own systems, that customer funds were not affected, and that it is notifying affected customers and regulators as the law requires.

## What we know and don't

Coinbase hasn't said how many customers were affected or which contact fields were exposed, such as email addresses or phone numbers. Posts on X claiming more than 70,000 users were hit have not been confirmed by Coinbase or Amplitude. Coinbase said other Amplitude clients were also affected. We found no public statement from Amplitude as of publication.

The Defiant reported the same account of the incident, citing Coinbase's statement.

## Why contact data still matters

Leaked emails and phone numbers are the raw material for phishing. Anyone who knows you hold a Coinbase account can pose as its support team, so an unexpected call or text claiming to be Coinbase deserves a check through the official app before any reply.

The open question is how many accounts are in Amplitude's "small subset," and whether Amplitude will say so itself.
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Robinhood's Event Contracts Out-Earn Crypto as Q3 Revenue Hits Record
articles.excerpt: Crypto trading volume fell 38% to $50 billion. Event contracts traded hit a record 16.4 billion, more than seven times last year's count.
articles.body_md:
Robinhood made more from event contracts than from crypto in the third quarter. Event contracts brought in $173 million, up more than sixfold, while crypto revenue fell 55% to $120 million, the company said Tuesday.

Total net revenue was a record $1.42 billion, up 12% from a year earlier. Profit went the other way.

For crypto readers, the slide shows up in trading as well as revenue. Robinhood's crypto notional volume (the dollar value traded) fell 38% to $50 billion. Volume in the Robinhood app dropped 48% to $21 billion, and its Bitstamp exchange fell 28% to $29 billion. The company said lower crypto prices also trimmed its platform assets, which still rose 19% to $396 billion.

**Prediction markets set the record**

Customers traded 16.4 billion event contracts, a record and more than seven times the year-ago count. Options revenue rose 31% to $399 million.

Net income fell 14% to $476 million, or 51 cents a diluted share, partly on $67 million of unrealized losses tied to its Robinhood Ventures Fund I. Adjusted EPS, a new non-GAAP measure, was 60 cents.

Robinhood Chain, in its first quarter on mainnet, produced over $50 million in chain fees and over $80 billion in DEX volume, the company said. It calls the network a top-five chain by revenue and volume.

October is off to a fast start. Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma said net deposits "have already topped $13 billion month-to-date," including $6 billion tied to the Dell family's Trump Accounts contribution.

Black Mint couldn't confirm the after-hours share move from a second source before publication.

*In our opinion: a year ago, crypto out-earned event contracts by more than $200 million. This quarter the order flipped, and the Q4 report will show whether it sticks.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: CFTC Sues Utah, the 10th State It Has Taken On Over Prediction Markets
articles.excerpt: Utah's attorney general sued Kalshi on Oct. 20, calling its markets illegal gambling. The CFTC says federal law gives it sole say over them.
articles.body_md:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah on Tuesday to stop the state from using its gambling laws against federally registered prediction markets. Utah is the 10th state the agency has moved against in court.

The fight is over who gets to police event contracts, the yes-or-no bets on real-world outcomes that users trade with each other. That reaches crypto platforms too: Robinhood reported $173 million in event contracts revenue for the third quarter on Tuesday.

**Utah went after Kalshi first**

Utah Attorney General Derek Brown sued Kalshi and related companies on Oct. 20 in state court in Salt Lake County, alleging its markets are illegal gambling. The suit also names two Susquehanna trading firms, the CFTC complaint shows.

The CFTC's complaint, filed Oct. 26 in federal court against Utah and Brown, argues that a contract paying out on an event is a swap under the Commodity Exchange Act. Congress gave the CFTC "exclusive jurisdiction" over those, the complaint says.

"Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets," CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said.

**What Utah says**

Brown said on Oct. 20 that "Kalshi runs an online casino in Utah and calls it a prediction market." A spokesperson for his office declined to comment on the CFTC suit, Utah Politics reported. Kalshi has rejected the gambling charge, Politico reported.

Courts have sided with Utah so far. In August, U.S. District Judge Robert Shelby ruled that federal law doesn't override Utah's gambling laws, and the 10th Circuit on Sept. 8 refused to pause enforcement while Kalshi appeals.

*In our opinion: the decision that counts sits with the 10th Circuit, where Kalshi's appeal is still pending. A ruling there would carry more weight than this new filing.*

articles.title: Keystone Tells Owners to Treat Wallets Received After Oct. 20 as Risky
articles.excerpt: A stolen factory authenticity credential means a fake device could pass Keystone's own check. The company is scrapping 18,835 unsold wallets and won't ask for recall shipments.
articles.body_md:
Keystone told owners on Tuesday that any of its wallets received after Oct. 20 "should be considered risky," a day after saying it will scrap 18,835 unsold devices.

The problem is WebAuth, an authenticity credential Keystone burns into each device at the factory to prove the hardware is genuine. The attacker behind the company's Oct. 20 website breach also obtained it, Keystone said in a [statement on X](https://x.com/KeystoneWallet/status/2114719318722404578) on Monday. A copy could let a counterfeiter build a fake that passes Keystone's check.

It can't be erased or rewritten after manufacturing. So Keystone is scrapping its stock, moving production to a fresh credential and holding unsent web orders, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/keystone-halts-web-orders-will-junk-18835-wallets-in-stock-over-stolen-authenticity-key/) reported.

**What owners should do**

Devices delivered before Oct. 20 can be trusted if they pass authentication, Keystone said. For devices received after that date that still carry the old credential, it said it can't rule out a counterfeit even when the check passes, and it asked owners to contact support before using them. "If you receive your Keystone after Oct 20, it should be considered risky," the company [wrote on X](https://x.com/KeystoneWallet/status/2115098871781298191).

WebAuth plays no part in recovery phrases or transaction signing, Keystone said. It added that it will never ask owners to ship a device back for a "recall."

**Data kept too long**

The breach exposed 25,964 buyer records from 2024 to 2026, plus 12,873 unpaid checkout records. Keystone said a faulty deletion tool kept some data past its 180-day limit. "We failed to fulfill our commitment to erase customer data on time, and we accept responsibility for this failure," it said. It is cutting retention to 90 days.

*In our opinion: the date on the delivery slip now matters more than the check on the screen. Anyone unsure should call support before moving funds onto a post-Oct. 20 device.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Janus Henderson Takes the Nasdaq-100 Onchain, but Not for U.S. Buyers
articles.excerpt: JQQQ is the manager's own fund, not a third-party stock token. The release gives no fee rate, minimum or start date for subscriptions.
articles.body_md:
Janus Henderson, which manages about $500 billion, launched a fund on Tuesday that tracks the Nasdaq-100 and lives only on the Stellar blockchain.

The fund, JQQQ, was built with tokenization firm Centrifuge.

The companies call it the first blockchain-native fund offering Nasdaq-100 exposure through an issuer-sponsored strategy. It is built to run onchain rather than mirror shares held elsewhere. Janus Henderson runs the strategy, Nasdaq licenses the index and Centrifuge supplies the onchain plumbing, [the companies said](https://www.janushenderson.com/corporate/press-releases/janus-henderson-and-centrifuge-launch-blockchain-native-fund-tracking-the-nasdaq-100-index-jqqq/).

**Closed to U.S. buyers for now**

The fund is open only to eligible investors where it can legally be sold. It is not available to U.S. persons. Legally, JQQQ sits inside Anemoy Capital SPC, a British Virgin Islands company, with a Janus Henderson U.S. unit as sub-manager.

The release calls the fees "competitive" but gives no rate. It also lists no minimum investment or start date for subscriptions.

Its risk section says tokenized shares carry extra risks beyond the stocks themselves, including failures of blockchain networks, smart contracts or wallets that "could delay or prevent transfers or redemptions."

**A $1 billion onchain shelf**

Janus Henderson said its onchain lineup now holds more than $1 billion across Treasuries, structured credit and stocks. Stellar's real-world assets passed $4 billion this year, the release said. Nasdaq's Sean Wasserman said "demand continues to grow for exposure to established, transparent benchmarks."

*In our opinion: the index is famous, but the price tag is still a secret. The fee line is the one to ask for when subscriptions open.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Ethereum Fixes Glamsterdam Flaw That Could Misroute Staking Deposits
articles.excerpt: A spec fix merged Monday stops a builder from claiming a staking protocol's deposit at the fork. It was closed a week earlier for lack of client support.
articles.body_md:
Ethereum developers merged a fix at 3:16 p.m. ET Monday for a Glamsterdam flaw that threatened to hand a staking protocol's ETH to someone else. They had closed the same fix one week earlier.

**How a deposit would have gone astray**

Under Glamsterdam, builders and validators both deposit ETH, tracked apart. The bug sat in the one-time step that sorts deposits still waiting in line when the upgrade switches on. Under the draft rules, once a pending deposit registered a builder, later deposits under the same pubkey went to that builder, whatever their withdrawal credentials said.

The researcher avsetsin, who filed the [GitHub issue](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/5735) on Oct. 12, gave an example. An operator queues a builder deposit. A staking protocol then funds a validator deposit under the same pubkey. If both are pending at the fork, "the operator can withdraw the protocol's funds," the issue says. No validator gets created, so the protocol can't produce the proof needed to recover the funds.

**Closed, then merged**

Maintainer Justin Traglia closed the [pull request](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5736) on Oct. 19, writing that "there was not enough support from clients to make this change at this time." Avsetsin added tests on Oct. 23, and Traglia reopened and merged it Monday. The new rule routes pending deposits by withdrawal credentials, so validator deposits stay with validators.

The flaw was in draft specs that have not reached mainnet. [CoinDesk reported](https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/10/27/ethereum-fixes-glamsterdam-bug-that-could-have-sent-staking-deposits-to-builders) that no losses were reported and that a planned Oct. 26 launch on the Hoodi test network was postponed. Client teams still have to ship the change.

ETH traded at $2,306 at 5:58 a.m. ET, down 1.2% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: a fix that loses the room one week and wins it the next is code review doing its job. Better to sort out the deposit line in a draft spec than on mainnet.*

articles.title: Binance Cuts 22 Tokens in Brazil as It Seeks Central Bank License
articles.excerpt: Brazilian users also lose eight products, including loans, margin trading and Launchpool, three days before the central bank's Oct. 30 filing deadline.
articles.body_md:
Binance ended trading in 22 tokens and eight services for Brazilian users on Tuesday, four days after it applied for a central bank license ahead of an Oct. 30 deadline.

The application went in on Oct. 23 through BBrasil Sociedade Prestadora de Serviços de Ativos Virtuais, a new group company, [Valor Econômico reported](https://valor.globo.com/financas/criptomoedas/noticia/2026/10/26/binance-entra-com-pedido-de-prestadora-de-servios-de-ativos-virtuais-no-banco-central.ghtml). It seeks authorization as a virtual asset service provider under central bank Resolutions 519, 520 and 521. Providers that file by Friday can keep operating while regulators review their paperwork, [Crypto Briefing reported](https://cryptobriefing.com/binance-files-brazil-crypto-license/). A filing is not an approval.

**What Brazilian users lose**

Binance [first announced](https://twitter.com/BinanceBrasil/status/2108336634324300179) the cuts on Oct. 8. The services going away are Binance Loans, Binance Pool, Cloud Mining, margin trading, Launchpool, Megadrop, HODLer Airdrops and Alpha 2.0, [crypto.news reported](https://crypto.news/binance-to-cut-8-services-and-22-tokens-in-brazil/). Open margin positions can stay open, but new margin orders and new borrowing stop. Outstanding loans move to repayment only.

The 22 delisted tokens include USDe, USTC, MANTRA, GMT, ZIL and STORJ. Holders can keep them or withdraw them. Spot trading in other tokens and stablecoins continues.

Customers are set to get local payment accounts through Binance Brasil Corretora, formerly the brokerage Sim;paul, by Oct. 29. New details will be required on international crypto transfers from Nov. 1.

Thiago Sarandy, Binance's general manager in Brazil, said the company supports regulation and hopes talks with the central bank will let it bring back some of the dropped products, per Valor. The central bank has not ruled on the application.

BNB traded at $735.05 at 5:58 a.m. ET, down 0.6% in 24 hours, per CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: the filing keeps Binance in Brazil, but the shorter menu is what local users feel today. The scoop to chase is which of the eight products the central bank lets back.*
articles.author: Blackmint Desk

articles.title: Euro Zone Mortgage Demand Sinks as Rates Bite, ECB Survey Shows
articles.excerpt: Banks expect housing loan demand to fall further next quarter. In a new question, they said digital assets will weigh on retail funding over the next year.
articles.body_md:
A net 27% of euro zone banks reported falling mortgage demand in the third quarter, the ECB said at 5 a.m. ET Tuesday. That was nearly double the 15% in the second quarter.

Banks had expected a drop of only 12%. The [ECB's bank lending survey](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr261027~506ef03145.en.html) polled 159 banks between Sept. 21 and Oct. 6, and all of them answered. "Increases in interest rates were the main driver of the decline," the ECB said, followed by weaker consumer confidence and housing prospects.

**Credit got harder to get**

A net 9% of banks tightened standards for business loans, more than the 5% they had expected. Consumer credit standards tightened by a net 14%. Demand for business loans fell by a net 6%, after banks had forecast a rise. Rejected applications went up for every borrower group.

The outlook is weaker. For the fourth quarter, banks expect housing loan demand to fall by a net 36% and consumer credit demand by 14%. France showed the sharpest tightening among the large economies, [Reuters reported](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/euro-zone-mortgage-demand-falls-as-rates-rise-ecb-survey-shows-ce785cddd88df121).

Not every number is dire. The ECB said the drop in mortgage demand "remains well below the peak" of the last rate-hiking cycle.

**A question about crypto**

The survey asked about digital assets for the first time. Banks said they helped their business strategy slightly over the past year. For the next 12 months, they expect a bigger lift to strategy but a negative effect on their retail funding business. Access to retail funding already fell by the most since the series began in 2011.

*In our opinion: the crypto answer is the line to clip. Europe's banks expect digital assets to help their plans and thin out their deposits at the same time.*

articles.title: Ripple Wins Final OCC Approval for the Trust Bank Behind RLUSD
articles.excerpt: Ripple says a federally supervised trust bank will manage reserves for its $2.5 billion RLUSD stablecoin, about 10 months after conditional approval.
articles.body_md:
RLUSD, Ripple's $2.5 billion stablecoin, is getting a federally supervised trust bank to manage its reserves. Ripple [said Monday](https://ripple.com/ripple-press/ripple-receives-final-occ-approval-to-establish-national-trust-bank/) that the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted final approval to Ripple National Trust Bank.

Issuance doesn't move. Standard Custody & Trust Company, regulated by the New York Department of Financial Services, will keep minting the token. The new bank adds OCC supervision on top. It will manage the segregated reserves, act as collateral trustee for RLUSD holders and offer digital asset custody to businesses.

RLUSD was worth about $2.58 billion near midnight ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ripple-usd). Ripple said it is backed by U.S. dollar deposits, government securities and cash equivalents, with BNY as primary reserve custodian.

"For years, we've said crypto and banks work better together. Final approval for Ripple National Trust Bank is what that looks like in practice," CEO Brad Garlinghouse said in the release.

**Ten months from conditional to final**

The OCC gave [conditional approval](https://www.occ.gov/news-issuances/news-releases/2025/nr-occ-2025-125.html) on Dec. 12, 2025, in the same batch as Circle's First National Digital Currency Bank, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets and Paxos. A trust charter isn't a full bank license. The bank can't take deposits or make loans, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-10-26-ripple-gains-final-occ-approval-rlusd-431810).

**Banks pushed back**

The Bank Policy Institute asked the OCC in an [October 2025 letter](https://bpi.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/BPI-comment-letter-re-OCC-NTB-application-re-Ripple-National-Trust-Bank-10-14-25.pdf) to reject the application. It argued that approving the charter would stretch the agency's legal authority, add new risk to the financial system and tilt the field against traditional banks that carry the full load of bank rules. That fight isn't new. The Independent Community Bankers of America has [also opposed](https://www.icba.org/web/payments/w/occ-releases-icba-opposed-national-trust-bank-chartering-rule) such charters for nonbank fintechs. We found no statement from either group on Monday's approval.

Ripple didn't say when the bank will open or what custody will cost.

*In our opinion: the date to chase now is opening day, and Ripple hasn't named one.*

articles.title: BlackRock and SBI Study Linking Tokenized Funds to a Yen Stablecoin
articles.excerpt: BlackRock signed an MOU with SBI and Startale to explore pairing tokenized money market funds with JPYSC, a $131 million yen stablecoin. No launch date was set.
articles.body_md:
BlackRock wants to see whether its tokenized money market funds can trade against a $131 million yen stablecoin. The asset manager signed a memorandum of understanding with SBI Holdings and Startale Group, the companies [announced Tuesday in Tokyo](https://www.startale.com/en/blog/blackrock-startale-sbi), Monday evening ET.

The target is JPYSC, a yen stablecoin issued through SBI Shinsei Trust Bank. Its market value was about $131.3 million near midnight ET, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/jpysc). BlackRock's dollar fund BUIDL was near $2.18 billion.

**How the pairing would work**

A money market fund holds short-term, low-risk debt. A tokenized version puts fund shares on a blockchain. A stablecoin can act as the cash side, so an investor could move between a fund that pays yield and a token used for payments without waiting on bank wires.

The partners will study three areas: technology, business and distribution, and regulation. SBI's [release](https://www.sbigroup.co.jp/news/2026/1027_16682.html) and Startale said the effort is open to other banks and businesses in Japan and abroad.

"The shift to onchain finance is becoming an unavoidable global trend," SBI Chairman Yoshitaka Kitao said in the announcement.

Japan set legal rules for stablecoins through amendments to its Payment Services Act, and the companies said the next step is building the infrastructure, distribution channels and regulatory frameworks that would connect tokenized assets with those coins at scale.

**What's missing**

The MOU is an agreement to explore.

It names no product, fees or timeline, and no JPYSC integration has been confirmed.

*In our opinion: an MOU is a promise to keep talking, and this one comes without a calendar. Watch who else signs up, since the door was left open for other banks.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Core Tags 32.1 Final, Ending Support for 29.x Releases
articles.excerpt: Version 32.1 raises the default peer cap to 200 and adds a mempool-based fee estimator. Details of three flaws fixed in 30.0 are due in two weeks.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin Core developers published version 32.1 on GitHub on Monday, along with maintenance releases 31.2 and 30.4. The 32.1 notes say version 32.0, tagged Oct. 21, was never fully released.

The reason given is "last-minute issues," with no further detail. So 32.1 is the first build of the new major series meant for node operators. It also starts a clock: the notes say versions 29.x and older are now at "End of Life" and won't get updates.

**Nodes get room for 200 peers**

The default cap on automatic peer connections rises from 125 to 200. The extra room goes to inbound block-relay-only peers, which pass along blocks but not loose transactions. Peers that relay transactions can fill at most half of inbound slots by default. Operators who want the old limits can set `-maxconnections=125 -inboundrelaypercent=100`, the notes say.

Fee estimates change, too. The `estimatesmartfee` command now blends the existing block-based estimator with a new one that reads the mempool (the queue of unconfirmed transactions). The release also fixes a possible leak of a sender's IP address in the experimental private-broadcast feature, under certain Tor setups.

The 32.1 notes credit 128 contributors.

**Three flaws to be disclosed in two weeks**

Under the project's security policy, developers plan to disclose three medium- and high-severity vulnerabilities fixed in 30.0. The notes don't describe them yet. The 32.1 download folder on bitcoincore.org returned "not found" at 6 p.m. ET, and the site had not posted an announcement.

*In our opinion: the number worth chasing is three. Those fixes go public in about two weeks, right as 29.x stops getting patches.*

articles.title: Strategy Skips Bitcoin for a Week as Strive Buys $511 Million
articles.excerpt: Strategy spent $204.9 million buying back STRC preferred shares instead of bitcoin, while Strive lifted its holdings to 43,000 BTC, Monday filings show.
articles.body_md:
Strategy bought no bitcoin from Oct. 19 to Oct. 25. It spent $204.9 million buying back 2,068,459 shares of its STRC preferred stock instead, according to an [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526431146/mstr-20261026.htm) on Monday.

Strive went the other way. It bought 6,182 BTC for about $511 million between Oct. 17 and Oct. 23, its [own filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1920406/000162828026067141/asst-20261026.htm) shows.

**Strategy's stack sits about 6.6% above cost**

Strategy holds roughly 848,517 bitcoin, bought for $64.02 billion at an average of about $75,446 each. Bitcoin traded near $80,400 at 11:57 a.m. ET Monday, per CoinGecko. The filing also shows no common stock sold through its at-the-market program, a plan for selling new shares into the market.

STRC is a variable-rate perpetual preferred share, so every share retired is one Strategy no longer pays dividends on. The buyback came out of "USD Cash," which fell to $242.4 million. A separate $4.83 billion reserve is set aside for dividends and debt interest. The filing doesn't say why Strategy paused its bitcoin buying.

**Strive paid more than today's price**

Strive's average price was about $82,732, roughly 2.8% above Monday's level. The purchases lifted its holdings from 36,818 to 43,000 BTC, while cash rose to $504.4 million. Strive also holds 505,000 STRC shares, valued at $50.2 million on Oct. 23.

*In our opinion: the number worth circling this week is zero, Strategy's bitcoin purchases. Strive, meanwhile, owns 505,000 of the very STRC shares Strategy was busy buying back.*
